olivia.meaning_en: Olivia is a feminine given name in the English language. It is derived from Latin oliva, olive. Both Oliva and Olivia were Latinate forms in use in English-speaking countries as early as the 13th century. Olive was in common use as a vernacular form.
olivia.meaning_fr: Olivia est un prénom féminin, principalement fêté le 5 mars avec sainte Olive.

emma.meaning_en: Emma is a feminine given name. It is derived from the Germanic word ermen, meaning "whole" or "universal". It likely originated as a short form of names such as Ermengarde or Ermentrude.

james.meaning_en: James is an English language given name that is a derivative of the name Jacob, most commonly used for males.
james.meaning_fr: James est un prénom masculin, variante de Jacques.

liam.meaning_en: Liam is a masculine given name, often a short form of the Germanic name William.
liam.meaning_fr: Liam est un prénom, diminutif de l'irlandais Uilliam, équivalent de l'anglais William et du français Guillaume. Le prénom Liam est apparu en France en 1986, et depuis, ne cesse d'augmenter année après année.

sophia.meaning_en: Sophia, also spelled Sofia, is a feminine given name, from Greek Σοφία, Sophía 'Wisdom'. Other forms include Sophie, Sofiya, Sofija, Sophy, Sophea, and Sofie.

aiden.meaning_en: Aidan, Aiden and Ayden are anglicised versions of the Irish male given name Aodhán. The Irish language female equivalent is Aodhnait.

mary.meaning_en: Mary is a feminine given name, the English form of the name Maria, which was in turn a Latin form of the Greek name Μαρία, María or Μαριάμ, Mariam, found in the Septuagint and New Testament.

hiroshi.meaning_en: Hiroshi is a common masculine Japanese given name. It can also be transliterated as Hirosi.

siobhan.meaning_fr: Siobhán est un prénom féminin irlandais. Ce prénom provient de l'anglo-normand « Jehanne », introduit en Irlande au Moyen Âge.

aadil.meaning_en: Aadil is a male given name.

aaliyah.meaning_en: Aaliyah is a female given name with origins in Hebrew that became popular in Arabic, making it a common given name for girls born to Muslim families. In 2007, an increase in usage was attributed to the fame of the American pop singer Aaliyah.

aamir.meaning_en: Aamir is a given name, a variant spelling of the Arabic name Amer, common to the cultures of the Indian subcontinent.

aaron.meaning_en: Aaron is an English masculine given name. The 'h' phoneme in the original Hebrew pronunciation "Aharon" is dropped in the Greek, Ἀαρών, from which the English form, Aaron, is derived. Aaron, the brother of Moses, is described in the Torah, the Quran and the Baha'i Iqan.

abbas.meaning_fr: Abbas ou Abbes est un prénom arabe et hébreu masculin qui signifie austère, sourcilleux ; il désigne aussi le lion.

abbey.meaning_en: Abbey is a unisex given name. Notable people with the given name include:

abbie.meaning_en: Abbie is a unisex given name. Notable people with the given name include:

abby.meaning_en: Abby is a given name, most often a shortened form of Abigail or Albert.

abdallah.meaning_en: Abd Allah, also spelled Abdullah, Abdhullah, Abdellah, Abdollah, Abdallah, Abdulla, Abdalla and many others, is an Arabic theophoric name meaning servant of God or "God's follower". It is built from the Arabic words ʻabd and Allāh.
abdallah.meaning_fr: Abdallah ou Abdellah ou Abdullah est un nom propre.

abdel.meaning_en: Abdul is the most frequent transliteration of the combination of the Arabic word Abd and the definite prefix al / el. It is the initial component of many compound names, such as عبد الحميد ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, عبد الله ʿAbd Allāh, and عبد الملك ʿAbd al-Malik.
abdel.meaning_fr: Abdel est un diminutif des prénoms de langue arabe composés sur le préfixe Abd-al, qui signifie « serviteur de ».

abdelaziz.meaning_en: Abd al-Aziz, frequently also transliterated Abdul Aziz, is a male Arabic Muslim given name and, in modern usage, surname. It is built from the words ʽAbd, the Arabic definite article and ʽAzīz "Almighty". The name is commonly abbreviated as "ʽAzīz".

abdelhafid.meaning_en: ʻAbd al-Ḥafīẓ is a Muslim male given name, and in modern usage, surname. It is built from the Arabic words ʻabd and al-Ḥafīẓ, one of the names of God in the Qur'an, which give rise to the Muslim theophoric names. It means "servant of the Guardian" or “servant of the preserver”.

abdelhamid.meaning_en: ʻAbd al-Ḥamīd, also spelled as Abdulhamid, Abdelhamid, Abd-ul Hamid, and Abd ol-Hamid, is a Muslim male given name and, in modern usage, surname. It is a Muslim theophoric name built from the Arabic words ʻabd and al-Ḥamīd, and thus means 'servant of the All-laudable'.

abdeljalil.meaning_en: ʻAbd al-Jalīl is a Muslim male given name, also used by Christians, and in modern usage, surname. It is built from the Arabic words ʻabd and al-Jalīl, one of the names of God in the Qur'an, which give rise to the Muslim theophoric names. It means "servant of the Exalted".

abdelkader.meaning_en: Abd al-Qadir or Abdulkadir is a male Muslim given name. It is formed from the Arabic words Abd, al- and Qadir. The name means 'servant of who can do everything'. Al-Qādir is one of the names of Allah in the Qur'an, which give rise to the Muslim theophoric names.
abdelkader.meaning_fr: Abdelkader est un prénom d'origine arabe, parfois aussi transcrit Abd el-Kader, et qui signifie « serviteur du Puissant ».

abdelkarim.meaning_en: Abdelkarim is a Muslim given name, variant of Abdul Karim, meaning "servant of the Most Gracious One". Notable people with the name include:

abdellatif.meaning_en: Abdul Latif is a Muslim male given name and, in modern usage, surname. It is built from the Arabic words ʻabd and al-Laṭīf, one of the names of God in the Qur'an, which gave rise to the Muslim theophoric names. It means "servant of the All-gentle".

abdelmalek.meaning_en: Abdul Malik is an Arabic male given name and, in modern usage, surname. It is built from the Arabic words Abd, al- and Malik.

abdelrahman.meaning_en: Abdelrahman or Abd al-Rahman or Abdul Rahman or Abdur Rahman or Abdurrahman or Abdrrahman is a male Arabic Muslim given name, and in modern usage, surname. It is built from the Arabic words Abd, al- and Rahman.

abderrahim.meaning_en: 'Abd al-Raḥīm is a male Muslim given name, and in modern usage, surname. It is built from the Arabic words 'abd, al-Raḥīm, one of the names of God in the Qur'an, which give rise to the Muslim theophoric names. It means "servant of the merciful".

abderrahman.meaning_en: Abdelrahman or Abd al-Rahman or Abdul Rahman or Abdur Rahman or Abdurrahman or Abdrrahman is a male Arabic Muslim given name, and in modern usage, surname. It is built from the Arabic words Abd, al- and Rahman.

abderrahmane.meaning_en: Abdelrahman or Abd al-Rahman or Abdul Rahman or Abdur Rahman or Abdurrahman or Abdrrahman is a male Arabic Muslim given name, and in modern usage, surname. It is built from the Arabic words Abd, al- and Rahman.

abdessamad.meaning_en: Abdul Samad Abdul Samed, etc. It may be roughly translated as "servant of the Self-sufficient Master" or "servant of the Eternal Refuge". Because the letter s is a sun letter, the letter l of the al- is assimilated to it.

abdirahman.meaning_en: Abdelrahman or Abd al-Rahman or Abdul Rahman or Abdur Rahman or Abdurrahman or Abdrrahman is a male Arabic Muslim given name, and in modern usage, surname. It is built from the Arabic words Abd, al- and Rahman.

abdoul.meaning_en: Abdul is the most frequent transliteration of the combination of the Arabic word Abd and the definite prefix al / el. It is the initial component of many compound names, such as عبد الحميد ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, عبد الله ʿAbd Allāh, and عبد الملك ʿAbd al-Malik.

abdoulaye.meaning_en: Abdoulaye is a West African masculine given name and surname. It is equivalent to the Arabic names Abdallah or Abdullah, given name of Muhammad's father. People with this name include:
abdoulaye.meaning_fr: Abdoulaye est un patronyme et prénom masculin d'Afrique subsaharienne, équivalent de l'arabe Abdallah ou Abdullah, prénom du père de Mahomet.

abdul.meaning_en: Abdul is the most frequent transliteration of the combination of the Arabic word Abd and the definite prefix al / el. It is the initial component of many compound names, such as عبد الحميد ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, عبد الله ʿAbd Allāh, and عبد الملك ʿAbd al-Malik.

abdullah.meaning_en: Abd Allah, also spelled Abdullah, Abdhullah, Abdellah, Abdollah, Abdallah, Abdulla, Abdalla and many others, is an Arabic theophoric name meaning servant of God or "God's follower". It is built from the Arabic words ʻabd and Allāh.

abdullahi.meaning_en: Abdullahi is a male given name also common as a surname. It is a variation of the Arabic personal name Abdullah. The variant Abdullahi is most common in Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, Somalia, and Ethiopia.

abdulrahman.meaning_en: Abdelrahman or Abd al-Rahman or Abdul Rahman or Abdur Rahman or Abdurrahman or Abdrrahman is a male Arabic Muslim given name, and in modern usage, surname. It is built from the Arabic words Abd, al- and Rahman.

abdur.meaning_en: Abdul is the most frequent transliteration of the combination of the Arabic word Abd and the definite prefix al / el. It is the initial component of many compound names, such as عبد الحميد ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, عبد الله ʿAbd Allāh, and عبد الملك ʿAbd al-Malik.

abdurahman.meaning_en: Abdelrahman or Abd al-Rahman or Abdul Rahman or Abdur Rahman or Abdurrahman or Abdrrahman is a male Arabic Muslim given name, and in modern usage, surname. It is built from the Arabic words Abd, al- and Rahman.

abeer.meaning_en: Abeer, also Abeir, Abbeir, Abbier or Abir is a feminine Arabic-language name meaning fragrance, aroma, perfume or a beautiful scent.

abel.meaning_en: Abel is a biblical first name which may derive from the Hebrew Hebel, itself derived from hevel, or from the Assyrian for son. In reference to the biblical story, Abel is usually linked with his brother who killed him, as in Cain and Abel.
abel.meaning_fr: Abel est un prénom masculin d'origine hébraïque se référant à Abel, deuxième fils d'Adam et Ève d'après la Genèse. La Saint-Abel a lieu le 5 août.

abhinav.meaning_en: Abhinava is an Indian male given name. The Sanskrit word abhinava has the meaning "new". Abhinava also means innovative, young, modern, fresh.

abhishek.meaning_en: Abhishek is a male given name that has its roots in the Sanskrit word abhiseka. The conceptual meaning of abhiseka is related to purification, cleansing or anointing.

abida.meaning_en: Abida is a feminine given name. The masculine version of the name is Abid. It means the one who worships.

abigael.meaning_en: Abigail is a feminine given name. The name comes from the Biblical Hebrew: אֲבִיגַיִל / אֲבִיגָיִל ʾĂḇīḡayīl, meaning "my father's joy". It is also a surname. The name can be shortened to Abbey, Abby, Abbie, Abbi, Abi, or Aby, as well as Gail and Gayle, among others.

abigayle.meaning_en: Abigail is a feminine given name. The name comes from the Biblical Hebrew: אֲבִיגַיִל / אֲבִיגָיִל ʾĂḇīḡayīl, meaning "my father's joy". It is also a surname. The name can be shortened to Abbey, Abby, Abbie, Abbi, Abi, or Aby, as well as Gail and Gayle, among others.

abigaelle.meaning_fr: Abigaëlle est un prénom féminin. Venant de l'hébreu abigahel qui veut dire « joie de son père » ou « source de joie », Abigaëlle, également orthographié Abygaelle, est un prénom féminin, fêté le 29 décembre.

aboubacar.meaning_en: Abū Bakr is an Arabic given name meaning "Father of a Young Camel" that is widely used by Sunni Muslims. Other transliterations include Abu Bakar, Abu Bekr, Ebubekir, Aboubacar, Abubakar, etc. The two parts of the name can be written together, hyphenated, or separately.
aboubacar.meaning_fr: Boubacar est un prénom masculin d'Afrique subsaharienne, équivalent de l'arabe standard Abou Bakr, prénom du premier calife de l'islam : Abou Bakr As-Siddiq, compagnon et beau-père de Mahomet.

abraham.meaning_en: Abraham is a given name of Hebrew background, originating with the Biblical patriarch; the father of the Abrahamic religions: Judaism, Christianity and Islam.
abraham.meaning_fr: Abraham est un prénom masculin d'origine hébraïque qui fait référence au patriarche biblique Abraham, personnage central de la Torah et révéré par les trois monothéismes dits « abrahamiques ».

abrahim.meaning_en: Abrahim is a surname and a given name, a variant of Ibrahim. Notable people with the surname include:

abubakar.meaning_en: Abū Bakr is an Arabic given name meaning "Father of a Young Camel" that is widely used by Sunni Muslims. Other transliterations include Abu Bakar, Abu Bekr, Ebubekir, Aboubacar, Abubakar, etc. The two parts of the name can be written together, hyphenated, or separately.

ada.meaning_en: Ada is a mostly feminine given name with the exception of the Turkish name being unisex. One origin is the Germanic element "adel-" meaning "nobility", for example as part of the names Adelaide and Adeline.

adalberto.meaning_en: Adalberto is the Romance version of the Latinized form of Germanic Adalbert. It is used in Italian, Portuguese and Spanish. It derives from the Old German Athala and Berth.

adam.meaning_en: Adam is a common masculine given name in the English language, of Hebrew origin. The name derives from Adam, the first human according to the Hebrew Bible. When used as noun, אָדָם means "man" or "humanity".
adam.meaning_fr: Adam est un prénom masculin et un patronyme d'origine très ancienne.

adanna.meaning_en: Adanna is a female name traditionally used by the Igbo people from the southeastern region of Nigeria. It's translated as “father's first daughter”. It is also regarded as a short form of Adannaya which means “her father's first daughter”.

adarsh.meaning_en: Adarsh is an Indian male name that denotes "an ideal".

addison.meaning_en: Addison is a unisex given name derived from the surname Addison. It has increased in use in the Anglosphere in recent years, perhaps due to its similarity to the fashionable name Madison.

addisyn.meaning_en: Addison is a unisex given name derived from the surname Addison. It has increased in use in the Anglosphere in recent years, perhaps due to its similarity to the fashionable name Madison.

adel.meaning_en: Adel is a given name of ancient European origins that evolved from words meaning "noble", "nobility" or "elite".

adela.meaning_en: Adela is a female given name, the latinate form of Adele, meaning 'noble' or 'serene'. Adela is a male name in Ethiopia, meaning 'favours', and a female name in Arabic. Notable people named Adela include:

adelaide.meaning_fr: Adélaïde est un prénom féminin français de forme savante, dont Alice représente la forme populaire.

adelina.meaning_en: Adelina is the Italian variant of Adeline, meaning 'noble' or 'nobility'. Its other variants are Adtelina, Adela, Adelia, Della, Adalyn, Adalynn, Adelyn, Alene, Aline, Delia, Aada and Ada.

adeline.meaning_en: Adeline is a feminine given name meaning 'noble' or 'nobility'; it is of German origin and derived from Old High German adal "noble". The root lives on in the New High German words Adel "nobility," edel "noble," and adelig "noble." It is related to the given name Adèle.

adell.meaning_en: Adel is a given name of ancient European origins that evolved from words meaning "noble", "nobility" or "elite".

adelyn.meaning_en: Adeline is a feminine given name meaning 'noble' or 'nobility'; it is of German origin and derived from Old High German adal "noble". The root lives on in the New High German words Adel "nobility," edel "noble," and adelig "noble." It is related to the given name Adèle.

adem.meaning_en: Adem corresponding to Adam, is a masculine given name common in Turkey, Bosnia and Albania.

adi.meaning_en: Adi is a Hebrew-language unisex given name, which means "jewel" or "ornament". It also means "my witness" in Hebrew. In Arabic, the title Adi was common in military distinctions in the early Islamic era. It means "the one who charges" in battle or sports.

adib.meaning_en: Adib is a given name and a surname meaning enlighted writer or one who practises adab. Notable people having this name:
adib.meaning_fr: Adib est un prénom de langue arabe qui signifie « le lettré, l'homme de lettres ».

adil.meaning_en: Adil is an Arabic masculine given name and surname. Adil is a variation of the name Adel, an Arabic male name that comes from the word Adl, meaning "fairness" and "justice". It is a common name in the Muslim world.
adil.meaning_fr: Adil est un prénom d'origine arabe dont la racine est dérivée du mot « Adl » signifiant « justice ». Le prénom en lui-même signifie « le juste, l'équitable ». Il est très utilisé par les musulmans ainsi que par les communautés chrétiennes arabophones du Proche-Orient.

adin.meaning_en: Adin is a male given name. In the Balkans, Adin is popular among Bosniaks in the former Yugoslav nations. In this region, the name is derived from the Arabic word دين, meaning faith. The name is also used as a modification of Edin.

adina.meaning_en: Adina is a female given name. In the Balkans, Adina is popular among Bosniaks in the former Yugoslav nations. The name is either a modification of the name Eden, which means "delight," or a modification of the name Edina, which is derived from the Arabic word دين, meaning faith.

adlai.meaning_en: Adlai is a male given name of Hebrew origin meaning "God is just". Notable people with this name include: Adlai H.

adna.meaning_en: Adna is a given name of Hebrew origin. Notable people with the name include: Adna Anderson, US engineer Adna Chaffee, Lieutenant General in the United States Army Adna R. Chaffee, Jr., major general in the United States Army Joseph Adna Hill, American statistician Adna R.

adnan.meaning_en: Adnan is a masculine name common in the Muslim world. Its eponymous bearer was Adnan, an ancient ancestor of various Semitic tribes. The etymological meaning of the name is settler, from a Semitic root `dn; "to stay, abide".

adolf.meaning_en: Adolf is a given name with German origins. The name is a compound derived from the Old High German Athalwolf, a composition of athal, or adal, meaning "noble", and wolf. The name is cognate to the Anglo-Saxon name Æthelwulf.
adolf.meaning_fr: Adolf est un prénom masculin en allemand, catalan, islandais, finnois, hongrois, néerlandais, norvégien.

adolfo.meaning_en: Adolf is a given name with German origins. The name is a compound derived from the Old High German Athalwolf, a composition of athal, or adal, meaning "noble", and wolf. The name is cognate to the Anglo-Saxon name Æthelwulf.

adolph.meaning_en: Adolf is a given name with German origins. The name is a compound derived from the Old High German Athalwolf, a composition of athal, or adal, meaning "noble", and wolf. The name is cognate to the Anglo-Saxon name Æthelwulf.

adolphe.meaning_en: Adolf is a given name with German origins. The name is a compound derived from the Old High German Athalwolf, a composition of athal, or adal, meaning "noble", and wolf. The name is cognate to the Anglo-Saxon name Æthelwulf.

adolphine.meaning_en: Adolphine is a female given name, the female equivalent of Adolf. People with the name include: Adolphine Fletcher Terry, American political and social activist Adolphine Kok, Dutch lawyer Adolphine Muley, Congolese Twa politician and activist

adolphus.meaning_en: Adolf is a given name with German origins. The name is a compound derived from the Old High German Athalwolf, a composition of athal, or adal, meaning "noble", and wolf. The name is cognate to the Anglo-Saxon name Æthelwulf.

adria.meaning_en: Adria is a feminine given name, a feminine form of Adrian. Notable women and fictional characters with this name include:

adrian.meaning_en: Adrian is a form of the Latin given name Adrianus or Hadrianus. Its ultimate origin is most likely via the former river Adria from the Venetic and Illyrian word adur, meaning "sea" or "water".

adriana.meaning_en: Adriana, also spelled Adrianna, is a Latin name and feminine form of Adrian. It originates from Italy and Spain.

adrianne.meaning_en: Adrianne is a given name. It is the feminine form of the male name Adrian.

adriano.meaning_en: Adriano is the form of the Latin given name Hadrianus commonly used in the Italian language; the form Adrião can be used in the Portuguese language while the form Adrian is used in the English language.

adriel.meaning_en: Adriel is a given name, derived from the Biblical nobleman Adriel. Notable people with the name include: Adriel N.
adriel.meaning_fr: Adriel est un prénom masculin. Il n’est pas fêté en France.

adrienne.meaning_en: Adrienne is the French feminine form of the male name Adrien.
adrienne.meaning_fr: Adrienne est un prénom féminin, équivalent du prénom masculin Adrien, issu du grec ancien adrianos, qui signifie « originaire de la ville d'Adria ». Ses dérivés Adria, Adriana, Adriette, Hadriana ou encore Drienne. Il a également donné son nom à la mer Adriatique.

aedan.meaning_en: Aidan, Aiden and Ayden are anglicised versions of the Irish male given name Aodhán. The Irish language female equivalent is Aodhnait.

aerin.meaning_en: Aerin is a given name. Notable people with the name include: Aerin Frankel, American ice hockey goaltender Aerin Lauder, American businesswoman

afreen.meaning_en: Afreen آفرین is a female name, usually given, meaning "Most beautiful", "Enlightenment", and Houri of heaven. Its origins lie in the Middle East. It is also used within the Persian language.

agata.meaning_en: Agatha, also Agata, is a feminine given name derived from the Greek feminine name Ἀγάθη, which is a nominalized form of ἀγαθή, i.e. the feminine form of the adjective ἀγαθός "good". It was the name of St. Agatha of Sicily, a third-century Christian martyr.

agatha.meaning_en: Agatha, also Agata, is a feminine given name derived from the Greek feminine name Ἀγάθη, which is a nominalized form of ἀγαθή, i.e. the feminine form of the adjective ἀγαθός "good". It was the name of St. Agatha of Sicily, a third-century Christian martyr.

agathe.meaning_en: Agatha, also Agata, is a feminine given name derived from the Greek feminine name Ἀγάθη, which is a nominalized form of ἀγαθή, i.e. the feminine form of the adjective ἀγαθός "good". It was the name of St. Agatha of Sicily, a third-century Christian martyr.
agathe.meaning_fr: Agathe est un prénom féminin, utilisé comme tel en français, danois, allemand, grec, norvégien, provenant du grec ancien αγαθος ou agathos, qui signifie « bon ». Similaire au prénom du poète Agathon d'Athènes.

aglae.meaning_en: Aglaé is a French female given name.

famous.name: Agnes of France, Duchess of Burgundy

agnes.meaning_en: Agnes is a feminine given name derived from the Greek Ἁγνή Hagnḗ, meaning 'pure' or 'holy'. This was Latinized Hagnes, and passed to Italian as Agnese, to French as Agnès, to Agnes in English and other Germanic languages, to Portuguese as Inês, and to Spanish as Inés.
agnes.meaning_fr: Agnès est un prénom féminin français. Il est fêté le 21 janvier.

agustin.meaning_en: Agustín is a Spanish given name and sometimes a surname. It is related to Augustín. Notable people with the name include:

ahmad.meaning_en: Ahmad is an Arabic male given name common in most parts of the Muslim world, since it is one of the well-known names of Prophet Muhammad. Other English spellings of the name include Ahmed, Ahmmad. It is also used as a surname.

ahmed.meaning_en: Ahmad is an Arabic male given name common in most parts of the Muslim world, since it is one of the well-known names of Prophet Muhammad. Other English spellings of the name include Ahmed, Ahmmad. It is also used as a surname.

ahmet.meaning_en: Ahmad is an Arabic male given name common in most parts of the Muslim world, since it is one of the well-known names of Prophet Muhammad. Other English spellings of the name include Ahmed, Ahmmad. It is also used as a surname.

ahna.meaning_en: Ahna is a feminine given name. Notable people with the name include: Ahna Capri, Hungarian-American actress Ahna Girshick, American artist, computer scientist and neuroscientist Ahna O'Reilly, American actress Ahna Skop, American geneticist and artist

aidan.meaning_en: Aidan, Aiden and Ayden are anglicised versions of the Irish male given name Aodhán. The Irish language female equivalent is Aodhnait.

aiko.meaning_en: Aiko is a feminine Japanese given name. Aikō is a Japanese surname, also romanized as Aikoh or Aiko. Aiko or Ayko is also a traditional masculine given name in northern Germany and parts of Scandinavia.
aiko.meaning_fr: Aiko est un prénom japonais féminin et un prénom germanique mixte.

aila.meaning_en: Aila is a female given name found in several different languages, It is the Finnish equivalent of Helga or Olga, meaning "holy, blessed". In Scottish Gaelic, it means "from the strong place". It is also a variant spelling of the Turkish name Ayla and the Hebrew name Eilah.

aileen.meaning_en: Aileen is an Irish feminine given name, a variant of Eileen.

aili.meaning_en: Aili is a Finnish, Sami and Estonian female given name, with the pronunciation [aɪliː]. It is the Finnish variation of the name Helga, via the Sami Áile, deriving ultimately from heilagr, meaning "holy", or "blessed". Ailikki is a diminutive.
aili.meaning_fr: Aili est un prénom féminin estonien, finnois et samis.

ailsa.meaning_en: Ailsa is a feminine given name, not to be confused with Alisa.

aime.meaning_fr: Aimé est un nom propre ou un adjectif pouvant faire référence à :

aimee.meaning_en: Aimée, often unaccented as Aimee, is a feminine given name of French origin, translated as "beloved". The masculine form is Aimé. The English equivalent is Amy. It is also occasionally a surname. It may refer to:

aimeric.meaning_en: Aimeric or Aymeric or Aimery is a male given name.
aimeric.meaning_fr: Aimeric est un prénom masculin, dérivé de Heimirich, d'origine germanique, composé de heim signifiant maison, et de ric, roi. De ce nom dérivent les prénoms Heinrich et Henri.

aimie.meaning_en: Aimie is a feminine given name. Notable people with the name include: Aimie Clydesdale, Australian basketball player Aimie Atkinson, English actress and singer Aimie K.

aina.meaning_en: Aina is a given name that is found in multiple cultures.
aina.meaning_fr: Aina est un prénom japonais féminin. Il peut s'écrire あいな en hiragana ou en kanji.

ainara.meaning_en: Ainara or Enara is a Basque language feminine given name meaning "swallow bird".

aine.meaning_en: Áine is an Irish language feminine given name. It means "radiance" and is the name of the Irish Celtic goddess of wealth and summer Áine. Notable people with this given name include:

aishwarya.meaning_en: Aishwarya is a Hindu Indian and Nepali male or feminine given name, which means "prosperity" and "wealth".

aisling.meaning_en: Aisling is an Irish language feminine given name meaning "dream" or "vision". It refers to an aisling, a poetic genre that developed in Irish poetry during the 17th and 18th centuries. There is no evidence that it was used as a given name before the 20th century.

aislinn.meaning_en: Aisling is an Irish language feminine given name meaning "dream" or "vision". It refers to an aisling, a poetic genre that developed in Irish poetry during the 17th and 18th centuries. There is no evidence that it was used as a given name before the 20th century.

aissata.meaning_fr: Aïssata est un prénom d'origine sénégalaise, fêté le 7 septembre.

aissatou.meaning_fr: Aïssatou est un prénom féminin d'Afrique subsaharienne, équivalent de l'arabe Aïcha. Ce prénom a été porté sous sa forme arabe par l'épouse préférée de Mahomet après Khadija, fille du premier calife Abou Bakr.

aitana.meaning_en: Aitana is a Spanish feminine given name. The personal name is derived from a Spanish place name, Sierra de Aitana.

aiva.meaning_en: Aiva Aparjode is a Latvian luger who competed from 1998 to 2006. She finished 18th in the women's singles event at the 2006 Winter Olympics in Turin. Aparjode's best finish at the FIL World Luge Championships was 17th at Nagano in 2004.

aiyana.meaning_en: Aiyana Mo'Nay Stanley-Jones was a seven-year-old African American girl from Detroit's East Side who was shot in the neck and killed by police officer Joseph Weekley during a raid conducted by the Detroit Police Department's Special Response Team.

ajay.meaning_en: Ajay, also transliterated as Ajai is an Indian masculine given name originating in Sanskrit ajaya "unconquered", "unsurpassed", "invincible". A related name is Ajit.

ajla.meaning_en: Ajla is a feminine given name in various areas around the Eastern Mediterranean. In Arabic it means the “brightest”, “most dazzling”, “most brilliant”, smart.

akai.meaning_en: Akai is the name of: Shuichi Akai, a fictional character in the manga series Case Closed Shuichi Akai, Japanese former footballer Takami Akai, Japanese illustrator, game creator, character designer and animator Saki Akai, Japanese professional wrestler Hideyuki Akai, Japanese footballer Akai Teruko, Japanese Onna-musha warrior Akai Terukage, Japanese samurai Akai Gurley, African-American man shot and killed by a New York City Police officer Akai Osei, British actor, dancer and musician, winner of the first series of Got to Dance

akari.meaning_en: Akari is a feminine Japanese given name.
akari.meaning_fr: Akari est un prénom japonais féminin qui signifie « brillant » ou « lumineux ».

akemi.meaning_fr: Akemi est un prénom japonais féminin. Il signifie « beauté naissante » ou « belle aube ». Ce prénom est surtout donné à des filles, mais il convient également aux garçons.

akhil.meaning_en: Akhil is a given name of Sanskrit origin, meaning 'entire' or 'whole'. The equivalent feminine name is Akhila.

aki.meaning_en: Aki is a surname, a given name, and a nickname. Aki is a common Japanese, Finnish and Nigerian given name. Aki is also a Japanese surname.
aki.meaning_fr: Aki est un prénom dans plusieurs langues.

akif.meaning_en: Akif, Akef, Aakif or Aqif is an Arabic masculine given name, meaning "focused, attached, intent, devoted". It may also refer to one who sits in itikaf during the last 10 days of Ramadan, devoting oneself to ibadah during these days and staying away from worldly affairs.

akiko.meaning_en: Akiko is a feminine Japanese given name.

akim.meaning_en: Akim is a given name, a variant of Akeem, Hakeem, or Hakim.

akin.meaning_en: Akín is a popular Nigerian male given name and surname of Yoruba origin. It means "The brave one, warrior, valor, valiant one, the hero.". The name Akín is distinctive, carrying a strong and meaningful undertone.

akina.meaning_en: Akina is a Japanese feminine given name.

akio.meaning_en: Akio is a masculine Japanese given name.
akio.meaning_fr: Akio est un prénom japonais masculin fréquent.

akira.meaning_en: Akira is a given name present in a few languages. It is a unisex, but predominantly male Japanese given name. There are several kanji for Akira.
akira.meaning_fr: Akira est un prénom japonais mixte. Ce prénom est fréquent[réf. souhaitée].

akiva.meaning_en: Akiva or Akiba is a Jewish-ethnic name, arising in Aramaic from Hebrew: יַעֲקֹב, and thus cognate to English Jacob.

akram.meaning_en: Akram, is a given name and surname, derived from the Arabic root word Karam, meaning "generosity". In the Arabic language, Akram is a comparative adjective and means "kinder." In Turkey and Eastern Europe, the name is also rendered as Ekrem/Eqrem.
akram.meaning_fr: Akram est un nom propre d'origine arabe utilisé comme prénom et comme nom de famille. Akram signifie "Celui qui honore". Exemple : هذ الرجل اكرم زوجته - Hadh al rajul akram zawjatuhu - traduction : Cet homme a honoré son épouse.

aksel.meaning_en: See Kusaila for the 7th-century Berber leader. Aksel is a masculine name, used predominantly throughout Scandinavia, a variant of Axel.

akua.meaning_en: Akua is an Akan female given name among the Akan people in Ghana that means "born on a Wednesday" in Akan language, following their day naming system.

al.meaning_en: The nickname Al is often short for Alfred, Albert, Alphonse, Alphons, Allen, Allan, Alan, Alyson, Alysson, Allyson, Alistair, Alister, Alex, Alexander, Alexandra, Alexandrina, Alexis, Alexa, Alphonso, Alfreda, Alfredo, Alice, Alec, Alexandria, Alessandra, Alessandro, Alberto, Alberta, Alicia, Alvin, Alyssa, Alisha, Aldrin, Alden, Aldo, Alisia, Alannah, Alejandro, Alejandra, Aldwin, Ali, Allie, Allison, Alwin, Alfie, Alaric or Aloysius.

alain.meaning_en: Alain is widely used as a personal name and is the French form of Alan but also exists in English-speaking countries:

alaina.meaning_en: Alaina is a feminine given name, the feminine variant of Alain or an alternative version of Alanna.

alan.meaning_en: Alan is a masculine given name in the English and Breton languages. Its surname form is Aland. There is consensus that in modern English and French, the name is derived from the nomadic Iranian people known as the Alans, who settled in Western Europe during the Migration Period.

alana.meaning_en: Alana, Alanna, or other variants, is a female given name. It is latinized feminine form of Alan and its usage is relatively modern.

alanah.meaning_en: Alanah is a feminine given name, a variant form of Alanna. Notable people with the name include: Alanah Bloor, English actress Alanah Pearce, Australian video game writer and journalist Alanah Woody, American archeologist and anthropologist

alani.meaning_en: Alani is a name with multiple, unrelated origins from different cultures. It is a Hawaiian name meaning orange. It might be considered a modern English variant of the names Alan or Alanna.

alanna.meaning_en: Alana, Alanna, or other variants, is a female given name. It is latinized feminine form of Alan and its usage is relatively modern.

alannah.meaning_en: Alannah is a feminine given name, a variant form of Alanna.

alaric.meaning_en: Alaric is a masculine Germanic given name that, broken into its parts, means Ala "everyone's" and ric "ruler". This has various forms in the several Germanic languages, such as Alareiks in Gothic and Alrekr in Old Norse.

alasdair.meaning_en: Alasdair is a Scottish Gaelic given name. The name is a Gaelic form of Alexander which has long been a popular name in Scotland. The personal name Alasdair is often Anglicised as Alistair, Alastair, and Alaster.

alassane.meaning_fr: Alassane est un prénom masculin africain ainsi qu'un nom de famille.

alastair.meaning_en: Alistair is a male given name. It is an Anglicised form of the Scottish Gaelic name Alasdair. The latter is most likely a Scottish Gaelic variant of the Norman name Alexandre or the Latin name Alexander, which was incorporated into English in the same form as Alexander.

alba.meaning_en: Alba is a unisex given name of Latin origin meaning "white". In Spanish, Italian and Catalan the name means sunrise or "dawn". In Spanish, Italian and Catalan speaking countries it is considered to be a female name. It can also be used as a surname or as a title.

alban.meaning_en: Alban is an Albanian, English, German and French masculine given name. The Albanian female version is Albana.

albert.meaning_en: Albert is a masculine given name. It is derived from the Germanic Adalbert and Adelbert, containing the words adal and beraht. It is also less commonly used as a surname. Feminine forms of the name, such as "Alberta" are relatively uncommon and are declining in use.
albert.meaning_fr: Albert est un prénom français d'origine germanique, fêté à différentes dates selon le saint auquel il se réfère. Albert est une forme savante reprise à l'allemand Albrecht, par l'intermédiaire du latin ecclésiastique Albertus.

famous.name: Princess Victoria of Hesse and by Rhine

albertina.meaning_en: Albertina is a feminine form of the given name Albert in multiple languages.

albertine.meaning_en: Albertine is a feminine given name, a French feminine form of the name Albert. It was among the top 100 names given to girls in France between 1900 and 1926, and remained among the top 500 names for French girls until 1957.

alberto.meaning_en: Alberto is the Romance version of the Latinized form of Germanic Albert. It is used in Italian, Portuguese and Spanish. The diminutive forms are Albertito in Spain or Albertico in some parts of Latin America, Albertino in Italian as well as Tuco as a hypocorism.

albin.meaning_en: Albin is a masculine Polish, Scandinavian, German, French, Albanian, and Slovenian given name, from the Roman cognate Albinus, derived from the Latin albus, meaning "white" or "bright". This name may also be a last name.

albina.meaning_en: Albina is a feminine given name from the Roman cognate Albinus, derived from the Latin albus, meaning "white" or "bright". There are masculine variants including Albin in Albania, Kosovo, Poland, Scandinavia, and Slovenia; and Aubin in France.

albion.meaning_en: Albion is a given name, usually masculine, from the poetical name for Britain, Albion.

alcide.meaning_fr: Alcide est un prénom masculin français, dérivant du grec ἀλκή / alkế, fêté le 2 juin. C'est aussi le nom d'un navire-corsaire du XVIIIe siècle et d'un personnage de la mythologie grecque.

aldo.meaning_en: Aldo is a male given name, commonly found in Italy. People named Aldo include:
aldo.meaning_fr: Aldo est un prénom germanique dérivé d'Ald qui signifie « noble », « ancien ». Dans sa version méditerranéenne, l'origine d'Aldo viendrait du diminutif du prénom italien Rinaldo, forme latinisée du prénom germanique Reynold , qui donne Renaud en français.

aldona.meaning_en: Aldona is a Lithuanian and Polish feminine given name.

aldric.meaning_fr: Aldric est un nom propre qui peut désigner un prénom masculin peu usité ou un patronyme.

aleah.meaning_en: Alia or Aleah is a surname and a feminine given name, in both cases variations of the name Aaliyah. Of Arabic origin, the name means "high" or "exalted". Notable people with these names include:

aleana.meaning_en: Aleana is a feminine given name, similar to Alanna and Alena.

alec.meaning_en: Alec or Aleck is a Scottish form of the given name Alex. It may be a shortened form of the name Alexander or a given name in its own right. Notable people with the name include:

aleck.meaning_en: Alec or Aleck is a Scottish form of the given name Alex. It may be a shortened form of the name Alexander or a given name in its own right. Notable people with the name include:

aleida.meaning_en: Aleida is a female given name. It, like the Dutch name Alida and their variations – Aleid, Aleide, Aleidis, Aleijd, Aleyda, etc. – is derived from the Germanic Adelheid. The medieval names are often translated to Adelayde or Alice in English.

alejandra.meaning_en: Alejandra is a feminine given name, the Spanish form of the English name Alexandra, derived from the Latin Alexandra and the Ancient Greek Alexándra. It is the feminine form of the Spanish name Alejandro. The name Alexandra was the primary rendition in Spanish.

alejandro.meaning_en: Alejandro is a masculine given name, the Spanish form of the English name Alexander, derived from the Latin Alexander and the Ancient Greek Aléxandros, meaning "defender of man". The name Alexandro was the primary rendition in Spanish.

aleks.meaning_en: Aleks is a given name and alternative form of Alec or Alex.

aleksa.meaning_fr: Aleksa est un prénom serbe de genre masculin dérivé du prénom Alexandre. Aleksa est un prénom très répandu en Serbie notamment grâce au poète Aleksa Šantić[réf. nécessaire].

aleksandar.meaning_en: Alexander is a masculine name of Greek origin. The most prominent bearer of the name is Alexander the Great, the king of the Ancient Greek kingdom of Macedonia who created one of the largest empires in ancient history.
aleksandar.meaning_fr: Aleksandar est un prénom masculin d'origine grecque antique, qui est la version serbe, croate, bosnienne, macédonienne et bulgare du prénom Alexandre. En macédonien, bulgare, ainsi qu'en serbe cyrillique, ce prénom s'écrit Александар.

aleksander.meaning_en: Alexander is a masculine name of Greek origin. The most prominent bearer of the name is Alexander the Great, the king of the Ancient Greek kingdom of Macedonia who created one of the largest empires in ancient history.

aleksandr.meaning_en: Alexander is a masculine name of Greek origin. The most prominent bearer of the name is Alexander the Great, the king of the Ancient Greek kingdom of Macedonia who created one of the largest empires in ancient history.

aleksandra.meaning_en: Alexandra is a female given name of Greek origin. It is the first attested form of its variants, including Alexander. Etymologically, the name is a compound of the Greek verb ἀλέξειν and ἀνήρ. Thus it may be roughly translated as "defender of man" or "protector of man".

aleksei.meaning_en: Alexey is a Russian male given name derived from the Greek Aléxios, meaning "Defender", and thus of the same origin as the Latin Alexius. Similar Ukrainian and Belarusian names are romanized as Oleksii and Aliaksiej, respectively.

aleksey.meaning_en: Alexey is a Russian male given name derived from the Greek Aléxios, meaning "Defender", and thus of the same origin as the Latin Alexius. Similar Ukrainian and Belarusian names are romanized as Oleksii and Aliaksiej, respectively.

alen.meaning_en: Alen is a male given name of European origin.

alena.meaning_en: Alena is a feminine given name. It may be either derived from the name Helene or as a diminutive form of Magdalena. In the Balkans, this spelling of the name is predominantly found among the peoples of the former Yugoslav nations, specifically among the Bosniaks and Croats.

alessandra.meaning_en: Alessandra is a feminina given name, the Italian form of the English name Alexandra, derived from the Latin Alexandra and the Ancient Greek Alexándra, is the feminine form of the name Alessandro. The name Alessandra has other forms in Italian, such as Alessandrina and Sandra.

alessandro.meaning_en: Alessandro is a masculine given name, the Italian form of the English name Alexander, derived from the Latin Alexander and the Ancient Greek Aléxandros, meaning "defender of man".

alessia.meaning_en: Alessia is an Italian given name, the feminine form of the male given name Alessio, the Italian form of Alexius. In Greek it is Alexia. It is a popular name for females in Italy and was the second most popular name for Italian girls born in 2006.
alessia.meaning_fr: Alessia est un prénom féminin d'origine italienne, dérivé du grec « Alexandros » signifiant « celui qui protège ». En 2013, il s'agit du 15e prénom féminin le plus donné en Italie. Son équivalent masculin est le prénom Alessio.

alessio.meaning_en: Alessio is an Italian male name, Italian form of Alexius.
alessio.meaning_fr: Alexis est un prénom français d'origine grecque.

aletha.meaning_en: Alethea is an English-language female first name derived from the Ancient Greek feminine noun ἀλήθεια, alḗtheia, 'truth'. Aletheia was the personification of truth in Greek philosophy. Alethea was not in use as a name prior to the 1500s.

alethea.meaning_en: Alethea is an English-language female first name derived from the Ancient Greek feminine noun ἀλήθεια, alḗtheia, 'truth'. Aletheia was the personification of truth in Greek philosophy. Alethea was not in use as a name prior to the 1500s.

aletta.meaning_en: Aletta is a Dutch feminine given name, related to Alida, Adelheid and Adelaide. Alette is a variant form that is also used in Norway.
aletta.meaning_fr: Aletta est un prénom féminin néerlandais et hongrois. La variante Alette est utilisée en hollandais et en norvégien.

alex.meaning_en: Alex is a unisex name, employed either as a hypocoristic or a standalone given name, derived from the Greek element ἀλέξειν, meaning "to defend" or "to protect." Universally recognized as a diminutive for Alexander and Alexandra, Alex has, in contemporary usage, established itself as an independent given name for both males and females.

alexa.meaning_en: Alexa is a female form of Alex. It is variously a given name in its own right or a short form of Alexandra, both of which come from the Greek name Alexandros.

alexandar.meaning_en: Alexander is a masculine name of Greek origin. The most prominent bearer of the name is Alexander the Great, the king of the Ancient Greek kingdom of Macedonia who created one of the largest empires in ancient history.

alexandra.meaning_en: Alexandra is a female given name of Greek origin. It is the first attested form of its variants, including Alexander. Etymologically, the name is a compound of the Greek verb ἀλέξειν and ἀνήρ. Thus it may be roughly translated as "defender of man" or "protector of man".
alexandra.meaning_fr: Alexandra est un prénom féminin fêté le 22 avril.

alexandre.meaning_en: Alexandre is a masculine given name, the French, Galician, Catalan, and Portuguese form of the English name Alexander, derived from the Latin Alexander and the Ancient Greek Aléxandros, meaning "defender of Mankind".
alexandre.meaning_fr: Alexandre [alɛksɑ̃ːdʁ] est un prénom masculin fêté le 22 avril.

alexandria.meaning_en: Alexandria is a feminine given name, derived from Alexander the Great and the towns he named, most notably the city of Alexandria, Egypt. Alexandria was the 352nd most popular name for girls born in the United States in 2021.

alexandro.meaning_en: Alexandro is a masculine given name that served as a calque for Alessandro in Italian and Alejandro in Spanish, while also existing historically in Portuguese, French, and other languages.

alexandru.meaning_en: Alexandru is a masculine given name, the Romanian form of the English name Alexander, derived from the Latin Alexander and the Ancient Greek Aléxandros, meaning "defender of mankind".
alexandru.meaning_fr: Alexandru est un prénom masculin roumain, équivalent d'Alexandre en français. C'est également un nom de famille présent surtout en Roumanie.

alexei.meaning_en: Alexey is a Russian male given name derived from the Greek Aléxios, meaning "Defender", and thus of the same origin as the Latin Alexius. Similar Ukrainian and Belarusian names are romanized as Oleksii and Aliaksiej, respectively.

alexia.meaning_en: Alexia is a female form of the Greek male given name Alexis that in turn is a variant form of the Latin name Alexius.

alexina.meaning_en: Alexina is a feminine given name.

alexio.meaning_en: Alexius is the Latinized form of the given name Alexios, especially common in the Byzantine Empire. The female form is Alexia and its variants such as Alessia in Italian. The name belongs to the most ancient attested Greek names.

alexis.meaning_en: Alexis is a given name of Greek origin. Like the name Alexander, Alexis derives from the Greek verb: ἀλέξειν, romanized: aléxein, lit. 'defend'.
alexis.meaning_fr: Alexis est un prénom français d'origine grecque.

alexius.meaning_en: Alexius is the Latinized form of the given name Alexios, especially common in the Byzantine Empire. The female form is Alexia and its variants such as Alessia in Italian. The name belongs to the most ancient attested Greek names.

alexsander.meaning_en: Alexsander is a male given name, is a replica in writing of the American phonetics of the name Alexander.

aleyna.meaning_en: Aleyna is a feminine Turkish given name. Notable people with the name include: Aleyna Ertürk, Turkish fencer Aleyna FitzGerald, Australian model Aleyna Özkan, Turkish swimmer Aleyna Solaker, Turkish actress Aleyna Tilki, Turkish singer

alf.meaning_en: Alf is a given name, nickname and surname. The male name Alf or Alv is derived from álf, the Old Norse for "elf". It is also the shortened form of various Spanish names with álf as their first part, notably Alfred, Álvaro, or more directly from Ataulf.

alfred.meaning_en: Alfred is a masculine given name of English origin, a modern descendant of the Anglo-Saxon name Ælfrǣd, formed from the Germanic words ælf, meaning "elf", and rǣd, meaning "counsel".

alfredo.meaning_en: Alfredo is a cognate of the Anglo-Saxon name Alfred and a common Italian, Galician, Portuguese and Spanish language personal name.

algernon.meaning_en: Algernon is a masculine given name which derives from the Norman-French sobriquet Aux Gernons, meaning "with moustaches".

ali.meaning_en: Ali is a common unisex given name and surname of multiple origins.

alice.meaning_en: Alice is a feminine first name with roots in the French and German languages.

alicia.meaning_en: Alicia is a feminine given name. It is a variant of Alice, which comes from the Germanic name Adalheidis, meaning "noble natured".

alicja.meaning_en: Alicja is a Polish language given name that is equivalent to Alice in English.

alida.meaning_en: Alida is a feminine given name, a common Dutch version of Adelaide until about 1960. It is a compound word: adal 'noble' + heid 'gleam, glitter'. The name was also common in Norway between 1860 and 1910 when immigration was frequent.
alida.meaning_fr: Alida est le diminutif d'un prénom féminin allemand et hongrois.

aliette.meaning_en: Aliette is a feminine given name. Notable people with the name include: Aliette de Bodard, French-American speculative fiction writer Aliette Opheim, Swedish actress

alim.meaning_en: Alim is one of the Names of God in Islam, meaning "All-knowing one". It is also used as a personal name, as a short form of Abdul Alim, "Servant of the All-Knowing".

alima.meaning_en: Alima is an African and Kazakh feminine given name. Notable people with the name include: Alima Boumediene-Thiery, French politician Alima Mahama, Ghanaian lawyer and government official Alima Moro, Ghanaian football player

alina.meaning_en: Alina is a feminine given name with multiple origins in different cultures. It might be a form of Aline, which originated as a shortened form of Adeline, meaning noble.
alina.meaning_fr: Alina est un prénom féminin, porté notamment dans les pays slaves et en Roumanie. C'est également un nom de famille.

alioune.meaning_en: Alioune is a masculine given name.
alioune.meaning_fr: Alioune est un prénom masculin d’Afrique subsaharienne, équivalent à Ali, prénom du cousin et gendre de Mahomet, époux de Fatima.

alisa.meaning_en: Alisa and Alissa are female given names, versions of Alice, used in Russia, Ukraine, Finland, Estonia, and other countries. Notable people and characters with these names include:

alisha.meaning_fr: Alisha est un prénom féminin, porté surtout aux États-Unis depuis la seconde moitié du XXe siècle.

alisia.meaning_en: Alicia is a feminine given name. It is a variant of Alice, which comes from the Germanic name Adalheidis, meaning "noble natured".

alison.meaning_en: Alison is a female given name in English-speaking countries. It was originally a medieval French nickname for Alis / Alys, an old form of Alice derived with the suffix -on or -son sometimes used in the former French nicknames. The Middle English form was Alisoun.

alistair.meaning_en: Alistair is a male given name. It is an Anglicised form of the Scottish Gaelic name Alasdair. The latter is most likely a Scottish Gaelic variant of the Norman name Alexandre or the Latin name Alexander, which was incorporated into English in the same form as Alexander.

alienor.meaning_en: Eleanor is a feminine given name, originally from an Old French adaptation of the Old Provençal name Aliénor. It was the name of a number of women of royalty and nobility in western Europe during the High Middle Ages.

alla.meaning_en: Alla is a Russian and Ukrainian female given name. The Eastern Orthodox Church usually relates the name with Saint Alla, the widow of a Gothic chieftain, martyred in King Athanaric's times.

allan.meaning_en: Allan, a variant spelling of Alan, is both a given name and an English and Scottish surname.

aloys.meaning_en: Alois is an Old Occitan form of the name Louis. Modern variants include Aloïs, Aloys, Alois, Alojz, Alojzy, Aloísio, Alajos, and Aloyzas.
aloys.meaning_fr: Aloïs est un prénom masculin pouvent être utilisé comme prénom féminin en France. Aloïs apparaît principalement dans les cultures tchèque et allemande.

alper.meaning_en: Alper is a male Turkish given name. It is composed of the two words alp and er. In Turkish, "Alp" means "stouthearted", "brave", "chivalrous", "warrior". The second, er means "soldier, male".

alperen.meaning_en: Alperen is a Turkish given name. Traditionally, it is interpreted as “brave saint” or “heroic mystic.” In a modern reinterpretation, the name has been adapted to mean “Wise and Warrior Wolf”, symbolizing a combination of intelligence, wisdom, and a fierce, fighting spirit.

alpha.meaning_en: Alpha is a unisex given name.

alphonse.meaning_en: Alphonse, also spelled Alfonse, is the French variant of the given name Alfonso. People called Alphonse or Alfonse include:

alphonzo.meaning_en: Alphons is a male given name recorded from the 8th century in the Christian successor states of the Visigothic Kingdom in the Iberian Peninsula. In the later medieval period it became a standard name in the Hispanic and Portuguese royal families.

alson.meaning_en: Alson is a given name. Notable people with the name include: Alson is a German-bred thoroughbred racehorse Alson S.

althea.meaning_en: Althea is an English female given name. It is a variation of the Greek name Althaea, which may be related to Greek ἀλθος althos. Richard Lovelace used the name in a poem that John Milton later alluded to in his own poem "Lycidas".

alton.meaning_en: Alton is a given name. Notable people with the name include: Alton Adams, first African-American bandmaster in the U.S.

alva.meaning_en: Alva is a unisex given name.

alvin.meaning_en: Alvin is a male given name in several cultures. In the Balkans, it is popular among Bosniaks in the former Yugoslav nations, as well as among Albanians. The name is a variation of Elvin, another name commonly used within these groups.

alvina.meaning_en: Alvina is an English female given name with the meaning "elf friend", "amicable", "friendly".

alvira.meaning_en: Alvira is a name. It is a Spanish surname; as a given name, it is sometimes considered a variant of Elvira. Notable people with the name include:

alwena.meaning_fr: Alwena est un prénom féminin d'origine galloise. Alwena et son dérivé breton Alwenna sont fêtés les 28 janvier dans le calendrier breton, et le 1er mars dans le calendrier français.

alya.meaning_en: Alya is a female name that originates from Ancient Greek, Slavonic, Hebrew, and Arabic. In Russia, Alya is typically used as a colloquial name by people named Albina, Alina, Alevtina, Alexandra, or Alla. It is formed in a manner similar to other colloquial Russian names.

alycia.meaning_en: Alycia is a feminine given name. The name is variant of Alicia, a form of Alice, and is ultimately from the Germanic name Adalheidis, meaning "noble-kind".

alys.meaning_en: Alys is a feminine given name.

alysa.meaning_en: Alyssa is a feminine given name with multiple origins. Alysa is an alternative spelling. As used in Western countries, the name is usually derived from the name of the flower alyssum.

alyse.meaning_en: Alice is a feminine first name with roots in the French and German languages.

alysha.meaning_en: Alisha also refer as protected from God is a cognate of the Spanish-language feminine given name Alicia, a variant of the French/German-language name Alice, which comes from Old English Æthelhādas or Æðelhādas, meaning noble or nobility.

alyson.meaning_en: Alyson is a given name, a variant form of Alison. Notable people with the name include:

alyssa.meaning_en: Alyssa is a feminine given name with multiple origins. Alysa is an alternative spelling. As used in Western countries, the name is usually derived from the name of the flower alyssum.

ama.meaning_en: Ama is an Akan feminine given name originating from the Akan people following their day naming system, meaning "born on Saturday". Day names are a cultural practice of the Akan people of Ghana.

amadeus.meaning_en: Amadeus is a theophoric given name derived from the Latin words ama – the imperative of the word amare – and deus.
amadeus.meaning_fr: Amadeus, du latin qui amat Deum, est la forme latine du prénom Amadéo en italien, Amédée en français, Theophilius en Grec : theos = dieux et philein = aimer. On le trouve dans différents contextes, souvent par référence à Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart.

amador.meaning_en: Amador, from Latin amator meaning "lover", is both a surname and a male given name. As a given name it usually refers to Saint Amator.

amael.meaning_fr: Amaël ou Amael est un prénom épicène celtique qui vient de maël signifiant « prince ».

amaia.meaning_en: Amaya is a female given name and surname of Spanish origins, derived from the village of Amaya and its neighboring mountain in Castile and León, Spain. The name of the village, in turn, has Indo-European roots and means "am" or "mother".
amaia.meaning_fr: Amaia ou Amaya est un prénom féminin basque. Le prénom est tiré du livre Amaya o los vascos en el siglo VIII écrit par Francisco Navarro Villoslada en 1879 où le personnage d'Amaya est central.

amal.meaning_en: Amal is a unisex given name of Arabic and Hebrew origin.

amalia.meaning_en: Amalia is a female given name, derived possibly from Germanic amal, with meanings "vigorous, active, work", specifically the woman's name Amalberga. Its popularity is attributed to the Belgian Saint Amalberga of Maubeuge.

amalie.meaning_en: Amalie is a feminine given name. It is a German variant of the name Amalia. It is derived from the root word 'amal', meaning 'work' in German, 'hope' in Arabic and 'water' in Scots-Gaelic.

amanda.meaning_en: Amanda is a Latin feminine gerundive name meaning "she who must be loved". It is common in countries where Germanic and Romance languages are spoken.

amandine.meaning_en: Amandine is a feminine French given name, a diminutive for Amanda.
amandine.meaning_fr: Amandine est un prénom français féminin qui vient du latin amanda : « celle qui est à aimer » et « celle qui doit être aimée ». Ce prénom est fêté le 9 juillet.

amarachi.meaning_en: Amarachi is an Igbo unisex given name which translates to "God's grace" in English.

amari.meaning_en: Amari is both a surname and given name. Notable people with the name include:

amariah.meaning_en: Amariah means "promised by God" in Hebrew. It was commonly used as a name of priests in the History of ancient Israel and Judah. It appear several times in the Hebrew Bible: One of the descendants of Aaron by Eleazar.

amaryllis.meaning_en: Amaryllis is a feminine given name derived from the Ancient Greek verb amarýssō, meaning "sparkle, shine".

amaya.meaning_en: Amaya is a female given name and surname of Spanish origins, derived from the village of Amaya and its neighboring mountain in Castile and León, Spain. The name of the village, in turn, has Indo-European roots and means "am" or "mother".
amaya.meaning_fr: Amaia ou Amaya est un prénom féminin basque. Le prénom est tiré du livre Amaya o los vascos en el siglo VIII écrit par Francisco Navarro Villoslada en 1879 où le personnage d'Amaya est central.

amberley.meaning_en: Amberley is a feminine given name. As a given name, it is considered a variant of the name Amber, with a sound pattern influenced by the popular name Kimberly.

amberly.meaning_en: Amber is a feminine given name taken from amber, the fossilized tree resin that is often used in the making of jewelry. The word can also refer to a yellowish-orange color. The name was in occasional use in the early 1800s, according to United States census records.

ambrose.meaning_en: Ambrose is a given name. It is derived from Greek ambrosios, meaning immortal, god-like; cf. ambrosia, food of gods. Notable people with the name include: St. Ambrose of Milan St.

ameer.meaning_en: Amir (also spelled Ameer or Emir; is a masculine name of multi-lingual origin.

amel.meaning_en: Amel is both a given name and a surname. It is most likely the Maghrebine variant of the Arabic name Amal, which means "hope." The variant is quite popular in countries such as Algeria, Tunisia, and Morocco. In Algeria, it was the 10th most popular name during the 1990s.

amelie.meaning_en: Amélie is a French feminine given name, ultimately derived from the Germanic name Amalia. The variant form Amelie is used outside the Francophone world, sometimes by French people.

amer.meaning_en: Amer is male given name. In the Balkans, Amer is popular among Bosniaks in the former Yugoslav nations. The name is a modification to the name Amir, which means "one who lives a rich and prosperous life" in Arabic. This region also has a female equivalent: Amera.

americo.meaning_en: Americo is a Portuguese- and Spanish-language given name, occasionally used as a surname and in other cultures. It is a variant of the name Henry. English diminutives or hypocorisms include Rico & Eric. Notable people with the name include:

americus.meaning_en: Americus is a unisex given name, a Latin version of the Italian name Amerigo that is ultimately derived from the medieval German name Amalric, meaning "home ruler." Americus is etymologically related to the names Amaury, Emery, Emmerich, and Henry and their variants.

amethyst.meaning_en: Amethyst is a given name derived from a semi-precious violet variety of quartz that is also used to make jewelry. Ancient Greeks believed the stone prevented intoxication. An amethyst is also the birthstone for people born in February. The name may refer to:

ami.meaning_en: Ami is a given name of Hebrew, Persian, Indian, Japanese, and other origins.

amicie.meaning_fr: Amicie est un prénom français féminin. II est fêté le 20 février ou le 30 août.

amil.meaning_en: Amil, is an Arabic given name, used among different Islamic peoples, such as the Persians and Azerbaijanis. The name is interpreted to mean "a hardworking person, doer, striver", among other similar descriptions. As a word it appears in the Qur'an.

amina.meaning_en: Amina is the loose transcription of two different Arabic female given names: ʾĀmina meaning "safe one, protected" ʾAmīna, the feminine form of Amin, meaning "devoted, honest, straightforward, trusty, worth of belief, loyal, faithful, obedient of Iman".

aminah.meaning_en: Amina is the loose transcription of two different Arabic female given names: ʾĀmina meaning "safe one, protected" ʾAmīna, the feminine form of Amin, meaning "devoted, honest, straightforward, trusty, worth of belief, loyal, faithful, obedient of Iman".

aminata.meaning_en: Aminata is a feminine given name.
aminata.meaning_fr: Aminata est un prénom féminin, équivalent du prénom arabe Amina porté par la mère de Mahomet, Amina bint Wahb. Le prénom Aminata, très populaire en Afrique de l'Ouest, figure parmi les 400 prénoms les plus donnés en France en 2016 avec une tendance stable.

amir.meaning_en: Amir (also spelled Ameer or Emir; is a masculine name of multi-lingual origin.

amisha.meaning_en: Amisha is a given name. Notable people with the name include: Amisha Patel, Indian Bollywood actress Amisha Sethi, Indian author, philanthropist, business leader, and model

amit.meaning_en: Amit is a Hindu and Jewish given name and a Jewish surname. In Hindi, Amit originates from the Sanskrit word amita, amita essentially is the negation of mita, which means "to measure". In Hebrew, Amit means "friend", "colleague", ״peer”, or "member of the organization".

amity.meaning_en: Amity is a feminine given name of English origin that means “friendship”. It comes from the Latin word amicus, which means "friend".

amory.meaning_en: Amory is both an English given name – derived from the Old German name Amalric via the French form Amaury – and a surname derived from it.

amparo.meaning_en: Amparo is a Portuguese and Spanish word that means refuge or shelter. Several places in the Iberian Peninsula and in Latin America are named Amparo, some associated with Our Lady of the Refuge. It is sometimes spelled Ámparo.
amparo.meaning_fr: Amparo est un prénom féminin espagnol et portugais.

amr.meaning_en: Amr is an Arabic male given name.

amy.meaning_en: Amy is an English feminine given name. It is the English version of the French name Aimée, which means beloved. It was used as a diminutive of the Latin name Amata, a name derived from the passive participle of amare, "to love".

ana.meaning_en: Ana is a version of the female given name Anna meaning "favour" or "grace". In Croatia, the name Ana was the second most common feminine given name, or among the top ten most common, in almost all decades for which there is census data.

anabel.meaning_en: Anabel is a feminine given name. It is the Spanish version of Annabel.

anabelle.meaning_en: Anabelle is a feminine given name.

anais.meaning_en: Anaïs, Anaís, or Anais is a feminine given name.

anakin.meaning_en: Anakin is a masculine given name usually given in reference to the Star Wars character Darth Vader, a hero turned villain whose original name was Anakin Skywalker.

anamaria.meaning_en: Anamaria is a feminine given name.

ananya.meaning_en: Ananya is the common English spelling of two Indian given names: the masculine अनन्य ananya and the feminine अनन्या ananyā. The meaning of name Ananya is "unique".

anas.meaning_fr: Anas, Anass, Anasse, Anès en arabe ou encore Enes en turc, est un prénom d'origine arabe qui signifie « l'homme », « le genre humain », également « l'ami », « le confident » ou « le compagnon ».

anastasie.meaning_en: Anastasie is a French feminine given name derived from the Ancient Greek name Anastasíā.

anatole.meaning_en: Anatole is a French male name, derived from the Greek name Ανατολιος Anatolius, meaning "sunrise." The Russian version of the name is Anatoly. Other variants are Anatol and more rarely Anatolio.

anael.meaning_fr: Anaël est un prénom épicène. En effet, bien qu'originellement masculin, aujourd'hui, il est également féminin. Pour une fille, la graphie Anaëlle est la plus commune.

ander.meaning_en: The masculine name Ander is a variant of the Greek name "Andreas". Other variants of the Greek name "Andreas" are Andrés and Andrew, as well as Anders. The masculine name Ander is a variant Basque form of Andrew. Notable people with the name Ander include:

anders.meaning_en: Anders is a male name in Scandinavian languages and Fering North Frisian, an equivalent of the Greek Andreas and the English Andrew. It originated from Andres via metathesis. In Sweden, Anders has been one of the most common names for many centuries, earliest attested in 1378.

anderson.meaning_en: Anderson is a given name. Notable people with the name include:

andi.meaning_en: Andy, also spelled Andye, Andee, or Andi, is predominantly a diminutive version of the male given name Andrew, and variants of it such as Andreas, Andrés, and Andrei. The form of the variation is based on the Scottish "-ie" diminutive ending.

andie.meaning_en: Andy, also spelled Andye, Andee, or Andi, is predominantly a diminutive version of the male given name Andrew, and variants of it such as Andreas, Andrés, and Andrei. The form of the variation is based on the Scottish "-ie" diminutive ending.

andre.meaning_en: André — sometimes transliterated as Andre — is the French and Portuguese form corresponding to the English name Andrew and is now also used in the English-speaking world.

andreas.meaning_en: Andreas is a name derived from the Greek noun ἀνήρ anēr, with genitive ἀνδρός andros, which means "man". See the article on Andrew for more information. The Scandinavian name is earliest attested as antreos in a runestone from the 12th century.
andreas.meaning_fr: Andreas est un prénom masculin dérivé du grec ἀνήρ anēr et du génitif ἀνδρός andros qui signifie homme.

andree.meaning_en: Andree or Andrée is a feminine given name.
andree.meaning_fr: Andrée est un prénom féminin, l'équivalent masculin est André. Elle est fêtée le 9 juillet en l'honneur d'Andrée Minutte, en religion sœur Saint-Alexis, sacramentine de Bollène, martyre, guillotinée en 1794 à Orange.

andreea.meaning_en: Andreea is a Romanian feminine given name. It is the feminine of Andrei, the Romanian form of Andrew.

andrei.meaning_en: Andrei, Andrey, or Andrej is a form of Andreas/Ἀνδρέας in Slavic languages and Romanian.

andreia.meaning_en: Andréia is a Portuguese feminine given name. For the ancient Greek term ἀνδρεία or andreia, see Courage. Notable people named Andréia or Andreia include:

andreina.meaning_en: Andreína is a female name of Italian and Spanish origin, given in the Spanish speaking country of Venezuela, and can refer to: Andreína Álvarez, Venezuelan actress, entertainer, comedian, and acting teacher Andreína Castro, winner of the Teen Model Venezuela 2007 pageant Andreína Gomes, Andreína Martínez, Dominican–American model and beauty queen who was crowned Miss Dominican Republic 2021 Andreína Mujica, Venezuelan journalist and photographer.

andrej.meaning_en: Andrej is the form of the given name Andrew used in Slovak, Croatian and Slovene.

andres.meaning_en: Andres or Andrés is a male given name. It can also be a surname. It is derived from the name Andreas.
andres.meaning_fr: Andres est un prénom masculin célébré le 30 novembre et dérivé d'Andreas. Ce prénom peut désigner :

andrey.meaning_en: Andrey is a masculine given name predominantly used in Slavic languages, including Belarusian, Bulgarian, and Russian. The name is derived from the ancient Greek Andreas, meaning "man" or "warrior".

andruw.meaning_en: Andruw Rudolf Jones is a Curaçaoan former professional baseball center fielder who played 17 seasons in Major League Baseball, most notably for the Atlanta Braves.

andy.meaning_en: Andy, also spelled Andye, Andee, or Andi, is predominantly a diminutive version of the male given name Andrew, and variants of it such as Andreas, Andrés, and Andrei. The form of the variation is based on the Scottish "-ie" diminutive ending.

anel.meaning_en: Anel is a male given name. In the Balkans, Anel is popular among the Bosniaks in the former countries of Yugoslav. The name is a modification of Anil, and it holds the same meanings: righteous ruler, just emperor, and to be remembered forever.

aneta.meaning_en: Aneta is a feminine given name, a Slavic variant of Annette.

anette.meaning_en: Annette or Anette is a given name that is a diminutive of Anna or Anne, and has been used as a name of its own since the Industrial Age. In Greek, the variant Anneta is used. Notable people with the name include:

ange.meaning_fr: Ange est un prénom mixte, du grec aggelos qui signifie messager, ange et dont la fête majeure est le 5 mai. Il a pour variantes masculines Angel, Angéli, Angelin, Angély et Anges, et pour composé féminin Marie-Ange.

angel.meaning_en: Angel is a given name meaning "angel". In the English-speaking world Angel is used for both boys and girls. Angel is from the medieval Latin masculine name Angelus, which was derived from the name of the heavenly creature.
angel.meaning_fr: Angel est un prénom masculin signifiant Ange ou Messager. Le prénom Angel peut être également féminin dans les pays anglophone et Ángel est masculin dans les pays hispanophones. Ces prénoms peuvent désigner :

angela.meaning_en: Angela is a female given name. It is derived from the Greek word ángelos, meaning angel from Greek belief systems. In the United States, the name "Angela" was at its most popular between 1965 and 1979, when it was ranked among the top 10 names for girls.
angela.meaning_fr: Angela est un prénom féminin d'origine latine chrétienne provenant du grec ángelos et signifiant messager. Ce prénom peut désigner:

angelica.meaning_en: Angelica is an English language surname and female given name and a variant of Angelika or vice versa.

angelika.meaning_en: Angelika is a variant of Angelica, derived from Latin angelicus meaning "angelic", ultimately related to Greek ἄγγελος – "messenger". The poets Boiardo and Ariosto used this name in their 'Orlando' poems, where it belongs to Orlando's love interest.
angelika.meaning_fr: Angelika est un prénom hongrois, polonais, grec et allemand féminin.

angelin.meaning_fr: Ange est un prénom mixte, du grec aggelos qui signifie messager, ange et dont la fête majeure est le 5 mai. Il a pour variantes masculines Angel, Angéli, Angelin, Angély et Anges, et pour composé féminin Marie-Ange.

angelina.meaning_en: Angelina is a diminutive form of the name Angela, a name derived from the Greek angelos meaning messenger and archangel. Notable people and fictional characters with this name include:

angelino.meaning_fr: Angelino est un prénom masculin hispanophone.

angelita.meaning_en: Angelita is a given name that is the diminutive of Angel or Angela in various languages.
angelita.meaning_fr: Angelita est un prénom féminin espagnol et portugais.

angella.meaning_en: Angella is a given name. Notable people with this name include: Angella Dravid, New Zealand comedian Angella Emurwon, Ugandan playwright Angella D.

angelo.meaning_en: Angelo is an Italian masculine given name and surname meaning "angel", or "messenger".
angelo.meaning_fr: Angelo est un prénom masculin italien pouvant désigner :

angie.meaning_en: Angie is the diminutive form of five different names in English. It can be the pet form of the feminine Angela or Angelina, the masculine Angus or Angelo or the unisex Angel. In Greece, the equivalent of the feminine name Angie is Angeliki.

angus.meaning_en: Angus is an English language masculine given name. It is an Anglicised form of the Irish and Scottish Gaelic name Aonghas, which is composed of Celtic elements meaning "one" and "choice". Short forms of the name include Gus, which may be lengthened to Gussie, and Irish Naos.

ani.meaning_en: Ani is an Armenian feminine given name given in reference to the medieval Armenian capital city of Ani. The name was among the top 10 most popular names given to newborn girls in Armenia in 2012. It is also a nickname.

anibal.meaning_en: Aníbal is the Spanish and Portuguese masculine given name equivalent of Hannibal, itself a latinization of the Greek name Hanníbas, derived from “ḥnbʿl” in the Carthaginian language, a descendant of the Phoenician Canaanite language in which the name's meaning is "Baʿal [is] my grace", a cognate of the Hebrew honorific Baʿal “master/lord”.

anica.meaning_en: Anica is a female given name used among Romanians, Serbs, Slovenes, Croats, etc. It is derived from Anna. A regional variant of this name is Ance, and it is closely related to the names Anicka, Anika and Anka.
anica.meaning_fr: Anica est un prénom féminin slovène, serbe et croate.

anicet.meaning_fr: Anicet est un prénom masculin fêté le 17 avril.

aniela.meaning_en: Aniela is a Polish feminine given name, cognate with the Greek-derived name Angela. Anielka is a hypocorism of this name. The name Aniela became popular in the 18th century mainly due to the Ursulines.

anika.meaning_en: Anika is a female given name of Arabic, African, Dutch, German, Hebrew, Māori, Sanskrit, and Swedish origin and is also an alternative spelling of the name Annika or Anikha

anil.meaning_en: Anil is a masculine name that can be found across the world in various cultures, nations and regions. A common theme across the globe is that the name holds strong weight and is used as a masculine name.

anis.meaning_en: Anis is a masculine given name and surname of Arabic origin. The name Anis is an Arabic name that developed in North Africa and is very common in Morocco. In the Balkans, Anis is popular among Bosniaks in the former Yugoslav nations. It is also popular among Albanians.

anisa.meaning_en: Anis is a masculine given name and surname of Arabic origin. The name Anis is an Arabic name that developed in North Africa and is very common in Morocco. In the Balkans, Anis is popular among Bosniaks in the former Yugoslav nations. It is also popular among Albanians.
anisa.meaning_fr: Anissa est un prénom féminin arabe qui signifie littéralement « aimable, sympathique » ou « mademoiselle ». Son équivalent masculin est Anis. Il est parfois orthographié avec un y, Anyssa, qui signifie « Celle qui est là pour toi » ou « Compagne ».

anissa.meaning_en: Anissa or Anisa is a feminine given name derived from the Arabic language أنس, meaning “to be friendly.” Lebanese Maronite Christians also use the name as a form of Agnes because it derives from Persian Anahid, Anahit or Anaïs, meaning ‘immaculate’.
anissa.meaning_fr: Anissa est un prénom féminin arabe qui signifie littéralement « aimable, sympathique » ou « mademoiselle ». Son équivalent masculin est Anis. Il est parfois orthographié avec un y, Anyssa, qui signifie « Celle qui est là pour toi » ou « Compagne ».

anita.meaning_en: Anita is a feminine given name. The name and its variants are now common worldwide, especially in regions where Indo-European languages are spoken, namely Europe, Iran, South Asia, and North America. Anita is a short form of the ancient Persian name Anahita.

anitra.meaning_en: Anitra is an Arabic-sounding female given name, originally invented in the 1860s by the playwright Henrik Ibsen for a minor character in his play Peer Gynt. It later became popular as a female name in Scandinavian countries.

anja.meaning_en: Anya, Ania or Anja is a given name. The names are feminine in most East European countries and unisex in several African countries.
anja.meaning_fr: Anja est un prénom féminin d'origine slave orientale, diminutif d'Anne ou d'Anna, signifiant grâce ou la grâce. Ce prénom est également en usage en Scandinavie, dans les pays germanophones ainsi que dans les Balkans et notamment en Slovénie.

ankit.meaning_en: Ankit is a male given name of Indian origin.

ankita.meaning_en: Ankita is a Sanskrit word meaning "Marked". As with any adjective in the language, it can take on a nominal form. The word is often used as a female name in Asian countries, atypically because of its extended meaning as "one with auspicious signs/engraving".

ann.meaning_en: Anne, alternatively spelled Ann, is a form of the Latin female name Anna. This in turn is a representation of the Hebrew Hannah, which means 'favour' or 'grace'. Related names include Annie and Ana.

anna.meaning_fr: Anna est un prénom féminin qui vient de l’hébreu Hannah. En français, Anna est une variante d’Anne, et en anglais, d’Ann.

annabel.meaning_en: Annabelle is a feminine given name of French origin, a combination of the Latin name Anna, which comes from the Hebrew word for grace, and the French word belle, meaning beauty.

annabelle.meaning_en: Annabelle is a feminine given name of French origin, a combination of the Latin name Anna, which comes from the Hebrew word for grace, and the French word belle, meaning beauty.

annabeth.meaning_en: Annabeth is a female English given name created from a combination of the names Anna and Beth.

annalise.meaning_en: Anneliese is a female given name of either German, Dutch or Nordic origin. It is a compound form of "Anna" and "Liese", a short form of "Elisabeth".

anne.meaning_en: Anne, alternatively spelled Ann, is a form of the Latin female name Anna. This in turn is a representation of the Hebrew Hannah, which means 'favour' or 'grace'. Related names include Annie and Ana.

anne-charlotte.meaning_en: Anne-Charlotte or Anne Charlotte is a feminine given name.

anne-marie.meaning_en: Anne-Marie is a French feminine given name. It combines the two respective given names of Anne, and Marie. It is traditionally associated with Christianity because it joins the names of Jesus's grandmother Anne and his mother Mary. It may refer to:

anouk.meaning_en: Anouk is a French female given name and Dutch diminutive of the female given name Anna.
