anushka.meaning_en: The names Anoushka, Anouska, Anuschka, Anushka and Annushka are diminutive forms of the female given name Anna, derived from the Russian diminutive Аннушка. Anoushka also means "grace" or "a favour" or "a flower" in Persian.

anwar.meaning_en: Anwar is the English transliteration of two Arabic names commonly used in the Arab world by both Arab Christians and Muslims: the male given name ʼAnwar, meaning "luminous" or the female given name ʼAnwār, meaning "a collection of lights".

anwen.meaning_en: Anwen is a Welsh feminine name. Notable bearers of the name are: Anwen Williams, fictional character in the BBC series Torchwood Anwen Keeling, Australian painter Anwen Muston, British Labour Party politician It is not a very common first name, though neither is it rare.

anya.meaning_en: Anya, Ania or Anja is a given name. The names are feminine in most East European countries and unisex in several African countries.

aoife.meaning_en: Aoife is an Irish and Gaelic feminine given name. The name is derived from the Irish Gaelic aoibh, which means "beauty" or "radiance". It has been compared to the Gaulish name Esvios, which may be related to the tribal name Esuvii and the theonym Esus.

april.meaning_en: April is a feminine given name taken from the month of the same name. It was the most popular month name given to girls in the United States between 1960 and 2000.

arabella.meaning_en: Arabella is a female given name, possibly of Greek, Latin, or Celtic origin.
arabella.meaning_fr: Arabella et Arabelle sont des prénoms féminins, d'étymologie latine : orabilis. En raison de la parenté de leur signification étymologique, on peut fêter Arabella à la Sainte-Osanna, le 18 juin.[réf. nécessaire]

araceli.meaning_fr: Araceli et Aracely sont des prénoms féminins espagnols.

aram.meaning_en: Aram is an Armenian patriarch in the History of Armenia, and a masculine name in Aramaic and Armenian. It appears in Hebrew and Aramaic as Aram, son of Shem, and in cuneiform as Arame of Urartu. The name is most predominantly used by ethnic Armenians.

araminta.meaning_en: Araminta is a feminine given name linked to the plant Amaranth.

arantxa.meaning_en: Arantza or Arantxa is a Basque feminine given name, meaning "thornbush". It is a hypocoristic for Arantzazu, which is derived from Our Lady of Arantzazu, a shrine of Mary, mother of Jesus, in Gipuzkoa. People with the name Arantxa include:

arda.meaning_en: Arda is a given name. In Turkey, it is used as a masculine name. In Turkish, Arda means sceptre, an ornamented staff carried by rulers on ceremonial occasions as a symbol of sovereignty, and latter, the Arda river, a very old Turkic name in Uyghur writings.

ari.meaning_en: Ari is a given name in many languages and cultures, for both men and women. It also may be a nickname for a wide variety of unrelated names.

aria.meaning_en: Aria can be a male, female, or even a unisex name depending on the country of origin. The Persian Arya is a male name that means "noble". Italian Aria refers both "air" and the melody, aria. In the Albanian language, Aria or Ari means "treasure" or "gold" or "of high value".

ariadna.meaning_en: Ariadna is the Catalan, Polish, Russian, and Spanish form of the Cretan Greek name Ariadne, which means “most holy”.

ariadne.meaning_en: Ariadne is a feminine given name of Greek origin. It is derived from the Cretan Greek words ari, a prefix meaning most, and adnos, meaning holy. It is often given in reference to the story of Ariadne from Greek mythology.

ariana.meaning_en: Ariana is a Latin feminine given name. Arianna and Ariane are the two most common variations. It derives from the Greek origin name Ariadne.

arianna.meaning_en: Ariana is a Latin feminine given name. Arianna and Ariane are the two most common variations. It derives from the Greek origin name Ariadne.

arie.meaning_en: Arie is a masculine given name. As a Dutch name, Arie is generally a short form of Adrianus, but sometimes also of Arend or Arent, Arnout or Arnoud, or even Aaron. As a Hebrew name, Arie is a transliteration of the Hebrew word or name אריה, which means lion.

ariel.meaning_en: Ariel is a given name from Biblical Hebrew אריאל Ariel that literally means "lion of God". The female form is אריאלה. In modern Hebrew, Ariel is primarily used as a male name. Common short forms of Ariel are Ari Arie and Arik for boys. It also appears as a surname.
ariel.meaning_fr: Ariel est un prénom masculin provenant du nom d'Ariel, ange dont le nom signifie « lion de Dieu » en hébreu.

arielle.meaning_en: Arielle is a feminine given name and an alternative spelling of the name Ariel.

arif.meaning_en: Aarif is an Arabic male given name that is common in Eritrea, Ethiopia, Saudi Arabia and Yemen. It later spread to other Muslim countries, such as Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Iran, Indonesia, Malaysia, Pakistan and Turkey as well as among Muslims in India.

arina.meaning_en: Arina is a Russian feminine given name, a variant of Irina. The Belarusian variant is Aryna, and the Ukrainian variant is Oryna.

arisa.meaning_en: Arisa is a feminine Japanese given name.

aristide.meaning_fr: Aristide est un prénom masculin français issu du grec ancien Αριστείδης. Il est fêté le 31 août.

arjun.meaning_en: Arjun is an Indian male given name, which means lustrous, shiny white, color of the lightning; of the milk; of silver; made of silver. It is also the name of the Arjun tree due to its silvery bark; Name of lndra, and of the third of the Pandava prince.

arlene.meaning_en: Arleen or Arlene is an Irish feminine given name and variant of Carlene or Charlene and in the French derived from feminine diminutive of Charles.

arlette.meaning_en: Arlette is a French feminine given name.

arlie.meaning_en: Arlie is a given name. Notable people with the name include: Arlie F.

arline.meaning_en: Arline is a female given name.

arlo.meaning_en: Arlo is a unisex given name. Some sources state it to be of Old English origin, meaning "endless energy"; it was first used by Edmund Spenser, who "evidently invented" it, as the name of a hill where the gods debate in his poem The Faerie Queene.

famous.name: Armand-Emmanuel de Vignerot du Plessis, Duc de Richelieu

armando.meaning_en: Armando is a masculine given name. It is a variant of the name Herman.

arnold.meaning_en: Arnold is a masculine German, Dutch and English given name. It is composed of the Germanic elements arn "eagle" and wald "power, brightness".

arta.meaning_en: Arta is a female name derived from the Albanian word artë, which means "golden". Arta is also The Old Persian equivalent of the word asha, which means "truth" or "righteousness".

artem.meaning_en: Artem is a male given name of Greek origin, deriving from Ἀρτέμιος meaning “pertaining to Artemis,” interpretable as “devoted to Artemis” or “one who is under Artemis’ protection.” The name is especially common in Ukraine and Russia, and is also used in Armenian with the variant of Ardem in Western Armenian.
artem.meaning_fr: Artem est un prénom masculin fréquent dans certaines langues slaves mais aussi en arménien.

arthur.meaning_en: Arthur is a masculine given name of uncertain etymology. Its popularity derives from it being the name of the legendary hero King Arthur. A common spelling variant used in many Slavic, Romance, and Germanic languages is Artur.
arthur.meaning_fr: Arthur est un prénom masculin. Il est fêté le 15 novembre dans la religion catholique en référence à Saint Arthur de Glastonbury.

artur.meaning_en: Artur is a cognate to the common male given name Arthur meaning "bear-like", or "of honour". It is believed to possibly be descended from the Roman surname Artorius or the Celtic bear-goddess Artio or more probably from the Celtic word *artos.

arun.meaning_en: Arun is an Indian male given name meaning dawn in Sanskrit. The name derives from Aruna, the aspect of dawn and charioteer of Surya. The following is a list of notable people with "Arun" as their first, middle or last name.

arvid.meaning_en: Arvid, Arved, Arnvid or Arvydas is a male given name, most common in Scandinavia but also in Iran and Lithuania. In Scandinavia it is derived from Old Norse Arnviðr and means "forest of eagles" or "eagle wood".
arvid.meaning_fr: Arvid est un prénom masculin scandinave dérivé du vieux norrois Arnviðr, formé des éléments arn « aigle » et viðr « bois, forêt ». Dans les pays nordiques, ce prénom se rencontre surtout en Suède.

arvind.meaning_en: Aravind is a common Indian masculine name meaning lotus. The name is of Hindu origin. Its variants include Arvind, Aravinda, Aravindan, and Aurobindo.

arya.meaning_en: Arya, also spelled Aarya, Aariya or Ariya is a name of Indo-Iranian origin. It traces back to the ethnonym and endonym Arya, used by the Indo-Iranians to identify themselves.
arya.meaning_fr: Arya, également orthographié Aarya ou Ariya ou comme Aryo ou Ario, est un nom indien et iranien. Le mot sanskrit Arya est un nom de famille et un prénom masculin et féminin, signifiant « honorable ». En Iran, c'est un prénom masculin populaire et un nom de famille populaire.

aryan.meaning_en: Aryan also spelled Ariyan, Arian, Aryann or Aaryan is a given name and surname that is popular in India and Iran. The name Aryan is derived from the Sanskrit meaning "noble and educated" in the Indian context while it is from Old Persian in the context of Iran.

ashwin.meaning_en: Ashwin or Asveen or Ashveen is an given name most commonly used in India. It is related to the name of the Ashvins, the divine twins of Vedic mythology, as well as to the name of the Hindu lunar month Ashvin.

assane.meaning_en: Ascene is an African given name and surname, also a derivative of Hassan, Haissene, Acene, commonly used in South Africa, Namibia, Angola, Senegal, Mali, Cote d’ivore, Malawi in Arabic.

assunta.meaning_en: Assunta is an Italian feminine given name meaning "assumption". It and another variant, Maria Assunta was originated from the Assumption of Mary, one of the four Marian dogmas of the Catholic Church. Notable people with the name include:

astra.meaning_en: Astra is a female given name. Astra is primarily used in the English language. It is of Old Greek and Old Norse origin. Old Greek origin: It is derived from the word 'aster' which means star.

astrid.meaning_en: Astrid is a given name of Scandinavian origin, a modern form of the name Ástríðr. Derived from the Old Norse Ássfriðr, a compound name composed of the elements áss and fríðr.
astrid.meaning_fr: Astrid et Astride sont des prénoms féminins d'origine scandinave.

asya.meaning_en: Asya is a given name with varied origins. It is a Turkish feminine given name meaning Asia. It is a Bulgarian and Russian diminutive form of the feminine given name Anastasia, meaning resurrection. It is also a form of the Arabic name Asiya, meaning 'melancholic' or 'wistful'.

atara.meaning_en: Atarah or Atara is a Hebrew feminine given name meaning 'crown'. In the Tanakh, it is the name of a wife of Jerahmeel. It has been used as a translation of the Yiddish name Kreine.

athan.meaning_en: Athan is a Greek male given name, which means "eternal life" or "immortal" or "rising sun". It can be a variant of Athanasios, and is of rising popularity among younger Greek parents in the Diaspora. The name Athan may refer to:

athanase.meaning_fr: Athanase, également translittéré comme Athanasius, Athanasios ou Atanacio, est un prénom français masculin d'origine grecque qui dérive de Athanatos, signifiant « immortel », formé de a- privatif et de thanatos, « mort ».

athanasios.meaning_en: Athanasios, also transliterated as Athnasious, Athanase or Atanacio, is a Greek male name which means "immortal". In modern Greek everyday use, it is commonly shortened to Thanasis, Thanos, Sakis, and Nasos. The female version of the name is Athanasia, shortened to Sia or Nancy.

athena.meaning_en: Athena is a feminine given name of Greek origin, often used in reference to the Greco-Roman goddess Athena, the goddess of wisdom, strategic warfare, and handicraft.

athenais.meaning_fr: Athénaïs est un prénom féminin français d'origine grecque.

atiya.meaning_en: Atiyyah, which generally implies "something received as a gift" or also means "present, gift, benefit, boon, favor, granting, giving". The name is also spelt Atiyeh, Attiah, Attieh, Atieh, Atié, Atiya, Atiyya, Attiya, Attiyah, Attyé, Ateya, Attua, Ateah, Antuya, or Atia.

atlas.meaning_en: Atlas is a primarily male name, usually given in reference to the character from Greek mythology. It has increased in usage in recent years for both boys and girls in the United States along with other mythological names, but is still more used for boys.
atlas.meaning_fr: Atlas est un prénom mixte. Deux figures de la mythologie grecques portent ce prénom : Atlas, l'un des Titans de la mythologie grecque ; Atlas, le premier roi de l'Atlantide d'après le Critias de Platon.

atticus.meaning_en: Atticus is a masculine name of Greek origin meaning "from Attica." The name is often used in reference to Atticus Finch, a heroic lawyer who represents an African American man accused of rape by a white woman in a racist Southern United States town in Harper Lee’s 1960 novel To Kill a Mockingbird.

attila.meaning_en: Attila is a popular masculine name in Central and Eastern Europe, Southeastern Europe and Western Asia. Primarily in Hungary, Turkey and Chuvashia.

attilio.meaning_en: Attilio is an Italian masculine name.

aubree.meaning_en: Aubrey is a unisex English name. It was common for men and women in the Middle Ages, but had lost favour for a time before experiencing a resurgence of popularity for men in the 19th century.

aude.meaning_fr: Aude est un prénom français féminin, fêté le 18 novembre.

audie.meaning_en: Audie, Audey, Audy; is a given name and a surname. Notable people with the name include:

audra.meaning_en: Audra is an English feminine given name, a modern variant of the name Audrey, which evolved from the Anglo-Saxon name Æðelþryð, which was derived from æðel, meaning noble, and þryð, meaning strength.

audrey.meaning_en: Audrey is a feminine given name. It is rarely a masculine given name. Audrey is the Anglo-Norman form of the Anglo-Saxon name Æðelþryð, composed of the elements æðel "noble" and þryð "strength". The literal definition of the word is “noble strength” or “strength from nobility”.
audrey.meaning_fr: Audrey est un prénom féminin d'origine anglaise, fêtée le 23 juin.

august.meaning_en: August is both a given name and surname developed from the Latin, Augustus. Derived from the Latin word augere, meaning "to increase", Augustus had the meaning "esteemed" or "venerable" and was a title given to Roman emperors.
august.meaning_fr: August est un patronyme et un prénom masculin dont l'origine provient du latin Augustus signifiant estimé ou vénérable, lui-même dérivé de augere signifiant à grandir. Le nom devient par la suite un titre donné aux empereurs romains.

augustina.meaning_en: Augustina is a female given name, a recent coinage of Augustus.

augustine.meaning_en: Augustine is a masculine given name derived from the Latin word augere, meaning "to increase." The Latin form Augustinus is developed from Augustus which means "venerable" and was a title given to Roman emperors.

augustino.meaning_en: Augustino is a masculine given name.

aurel.meaning_en: Aurel is a Romanian-language masculine given name derived from Latin "Aurelius". The country with the largest proportion of people named Aurel is Albania with 0.1209% of the population. Following is Romania and France.

avery.meaning_en: Avery is traditionally a male given name ultimately derived from the Old English name Ælfred, which is formed from the elements ælf 'elf' and ræd 'counsel', and literally translates to 'elf-counsel'.

avie.meaning_en: Avie is a female or male given name. As a nickname, it can be short for Avis, Avery, Avanel, and Ava.

avigail.meaning_en: Avigail is a Hebrew feminine given name, the native Hebrew spelling of "Abigail".

aviva.meaning_en: Aviva is a female first name. It is a modern Hebrew name which translates to 'spring' or 'springtime'.

axel.meaning_fr: Axel est un prénom européen masculin, dont la forme féminine est Axelle, fêté le 21 mars.

axelle.meaning_fr: Axel est un prénom européen masculin, dont la forme féminine est Axelle, fêté le 21 mars.

ayden.meaning_en: Aidan, Aiden and Ayden are anglicised versions of the Irish male given name Aodhán. The Irish language female equivalent is Aodhnait.

aydin.meaning_en: Aydın, also spelled Ajdin, Aiden, Ayden, Aydin, or Aydan, is a male given name. In Turkic languages, the name means 'enlightened' and 'bright'; it is also commonly used for intellectuals. In the Balkans, the variant Ajdin is popular among Bosniaks in the former Yugoslav nations.

ayiana.meaning_fr: Ayiana est un prénom féminin d'origine amérindienne.

aylin.meaning_en: Aylin, also spelled as Aelyn, Aelin, Ailin, Ailyn, Ailynn, Aylinn and Eylin, is a female Turkish given name. It is sometimes used as a given name in the English-speaking world in modern times. The name Aylin means "moon halo" or "the one that belongs to the moon".

aysel.meaning_en: Aysel is a feminine Turkish given name popular in Turkey and Azerbaijan. In Turkish, "Aysel" comes from Ay-sili and means beautiful moon or moon beauty.

ayumi.meaning_en: Ayumi is a feminine Japanese given name. It is rarely used as a surname.

ayyub.meaning_en: Ayyub is the Arabic name of the Abrahamic prophet Job. Here it refers to the Islamic prophet which is mentioned in the Quran, see Job in Islam.

azalea.meaning_en: Azalea is an English name taken from the flower name, which is derived from the Greek word azaleos, meaning dry.

aziz.meaning_en: Aziz is a Semitic name from the root two-zayin. In the Hebrew Bible, the root two-zayin means 'reputable, powerful, sublime'. In the 1 Chronicles, Aziz was the son of Shema and the father of Bela.

aziza.meaning_fr: Aziza est en outre un nom arabe. La forme masculine de ce nom est Aziz.

azucena.meaning_en: Azucena is a Spanish surname and a feminine given name meaning "madonna lily", a flower that is a symbol of Mary, mother of Jesus. Notable people with the name include:

azura.meaning_en: Azura is a feminine given name meaning "blue", derived from a Persian word meaning "blue semiprecious stone" or lapis lazuli. Notable people with the name include: Azurá Stevens, American professional basketball player Azura Skye, stage name of American actress Azura Storozynski

baba.meaning_en: Baba can be a surname in several cultures such as Dravidian, Japanese, Turkics, and Yoruba. It is also a nickname for 'father' in some languages, and translates to "father" in the Arabic, Persian and Shona languages. In various Slavic languages “baba” means an “old lady”.

babette.meaning_en: Babette is a feminine given name, a pet form of Barbara.

bachir.meaning_fr: Béchir, Bechir ou Bachir est un prénom et un nom arabe, بشير, signifiant « celui qui apporte de bonnes nouvelles » : c'est l'un des noms qui désignent le Prophète. Il se rapproche du prénom français Ange.

bahar.meaning_en: Bahar in Persian appears as a feminine given name in Iran, Afghanistan and Turkey. It comes from the Middle Persian whʾl, which ultimately comes from Proto-Indo-European *wósr̥. A similar name also appears in the Semitic languages albeit with a different meaning.

bahia.meaning_fr: Bahia, transcrit aussi Bahiya, est un prénom arabe féminin.

bailey.meaning_en: Bailey is a given name derived from the surname Bailey. The most likely derivation of the surname is from bailli, the Anglo-Norman equivalent of bailiff. An early American bearer of the given name was Bailey Bartlett.

baldomero.meaning_en: Baldomero is a given name. Notable people with the name include: Baldomero Aguinaldo, a leader of the Philippine Revolution. Baldomero Espartero, Prince of Vergara, a Spanish general and political figure.

ballard.meaning_en: Ballard is a given name. Notable people with the name include: Ballard Berkeley, English actor Ballard Campbell, American historian Ballard MacDonald, American lyricist Ballard Smith, American sports executive, district attorney Ballard Smith, American politician

balthazar.meaning_fr: Balthazar est un prénom masculin utilisé en français, en anglais et en néerlandais. La forme « Balthasar » existe en allemand, les formes « Baltazar » et « Baltasar » existent notamment en espagnol.

banks.meaning_en: Banks is a given name of English origin that is a transferred use of a surname or place name that means “by a bank.” It also has modern associations with wealth due to the name for a financial institution and the family surname of the family in the Mary Poppins books and the 1964 film and its 2018 sequel and to Banksy, a pseudonymous England-based street artist and political activist.

baptiste.meaning_en: Baptiste is a French given name or surname, and may be a shortened form of Jean-Baptiste.

baraka.meaning_en: Baraka is a male given name.

barb.meaning_en: Barb is a feminine given name, often a short form of Barbara. It is also sometimes a surname.

barbara.meaning_fr: Barbara est un prénom féminin issu du grec barbaros, qui signifie « celui qui ne parle pas le grec » et par extension, « étranger ». Religion catholique Il a été repris tel quel en latin.

barbra.meaning_en: Barbara and Barbra are given names. They are the feminine form of the Greek word barbaros meaning "stranger" or "foreign". In Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox tradition, Saint Barbara was imprisoned in a tower by her father.

bartosz.meaning_en: Bartosz is a Polish given name and a surname derived from Bartłomiej, the Polish cognate of Bartholomew.

chasity.meaning_en: Chasity is an English feminine given name, either a variant of the name Chastity or a combination of the names Charity and Chastity.

chastity.meaning_en: Chastity is a feminine given name meaning chastity, referring to the virtue of exercising self-control over one's sexual behavior, which might mean practicing celibacy for a person who is unmarried, or monogamy for a person who is married.

chava.meaning_en: Eve is a feminine English given name, derived from the Latin name Eva, in turn originating with the Hebrew חַוָּה‎. In Greece the name Eve is Evi, a diminutive of the baptismal name Paraskevi.

chay.meaning_en: Chay is a masculine name. It is either a diminutive of Charles, ultimately derived from Germanic Karal, Karel, Karl, meaning “man”, or it may be Gaelic in origin, meaning “Fairy Tale”.

chayce.meaning_en: Chayce is a given name. Notable people with the name include: Chayce Beckham, American singer-songwriter, winner of season 19 of the talent series American Idol Chayce Jones, Australian rules footballer

chaz.meaning_en: Chaz is an English masculine given name or nickname, originally derived from a short form of Charles, although it is also used occasionally as a short form of other given names such as Chastity or Charlton. Notable people referred to by this name include the following:

chee.meaning_en: Chee is a unisex given name. Notable people with the name include: Chee Dodge, American politician Chee Soo, English writer

cheick.meaning_en: Cheick is a male Malian given name.

chelsea.meaning_en: Chelsea is an English given name derived from the Old English place name ċealc hȳð, or the modern Celcyth, meaning chalk landing place. The name evolved to Chelsea, a location on the River Thames that became a London borough known for its wealthy, socially influential residents.

cheri.meaning_en: Cheri is a feminine given name inspired by the French chérie, meaning darling. It has also been used as a diminutive of names starting with or containing the sound Cher- or Sher- such as Cherilyn, Cheryl, Sharon, or Sherilyn for females.

cherie.meaning_en: Cherie is an English female given name. It comes from the French chérie, meaning darling. It has also been used as a diminutive of names starting with or containing the sound Cher- or Sher- such as Cherilyn, Cheryl, Sharon, or Sherilyn for females.

cherilyn.meaning_en: Cherilyn is a feminine given name, an elaboration of the name Cheryl in combination with the suffix -lyn.

cherine.meaning_en: Cherine is a female given name. Notable people with the name include: Chérine, Belgian singer Cherine Abdellaoui, Algerian Paralympic judoka Cherine Anderson, Jamaican actress and vocalist Cherine Fahd, Australian artist Cherine Alexander, Miss Continental 1984

cherith.meaning_en: Cherith is a feminine given name. Notable people with the name include: Cherith Baldry, British children's author Cherith Norman Chalet, American diplomat Cherith McKinstry, Irish painter and sculptor

cherry.meaning_en: Cherry is a given name with multiple origins. In some instances, the given name is a transferred use of the surname Cherry. In other instances, the name was given in reference to the fruit. In other instances, it was an English version of the French term of endearment chérie.

cherryl.meaning_en: Cheryl is a feminine given name with multiple origins. The name might have originated as a combination of the name Beryl with the prefix Cher- from the French chérie, meaning darling.

cheryl.meaning_en: Cheryl is a feminine given name with multiple origins. The name might have originated as a combination of the name Beryl with the prefix Cher- from the French chérie, meaning darling.

cheryll.meaning_en: Cheryl is a feminine given name with multiple origins. The name might have originated as a combination of the name Beryl with the prefix Cher- from the French chérie, meaning darling.

chester.meaning_en: Chester is a masculine given name of English origins with Latin roots. It comes from the word "castrum", which means fort or encampment.

chet.meaning_en: Chet is a male given name, often a nickname for Chester, which means fortress or camp. It is an uncommon name of English origin, and originated as a surname to identify people from the city of Chester, England.

cheyenne.meaning_en: Cheyenne is a unisex name of Lakota origin, though it is more commonly used by females than males. The origin of the word is uncertain, though it may be derived from the Lakota language, from the word Šahíyena.

chiamaka.meaning_en: Chiamaka is a feminine given name of Igbo origin, meaning “God is beautiful”. Masculine use, though not unheard of, is extremely rare.

chiara.meaning_en: Chiara is both a feminine Italian given name and a surname meaning bright. Notable people with the name include:

chidera.meaning_en: Chidera is a name given by the Igbo people of South-Eastern Nigeria, and is applicable to both sexes. It means “once God has written”, a more specific variant of “Odera”. A diminutive version of the name is “Dera”.

chinyere.meaning_en: Chinyere is a common Igbo given name that means “God provides”. It can be an element in longer names, such as Nkechinyere. It is unisex, but more common for girls.
chinyere.meaning_fr: Chinyere est un prénom féminin d'origine nigériane.

chip.meaning_en: Chip is an English given name and nickname in the United States, which is often a diminutive form of Charles or Christopher. Notable people referred to by this name include the following:

chisom.meaning_en: Chisom is an Igbo given name. It means "God follows me".

chiyoko.meaning_en: Chiyoko is a feminine Japanese given name.

chloe.meaning_en: Chloe, also spelled Chloë, Chlöe, or Chloé, is a feminine name meaning "blooming" or "fertility" in Greek. The name ultimately derives, through Greek, from the Proto-Indo-European root *ǵʰelh₃-, which relates to the colors yellow and green.
chloe.meaning_fr: Chloé est un prénom français dérivé du grec Χλόη, qui signifie « la verdoyante », « herbe naissante », « pousse nouvelle d’un vert clair », « verdure nouvelle » ou encore « jeune pousse ». Il peut s'écrire en français de différentes manières : Cloé, Chloé, Chloë ou Khloé.

chris.meaning_en: Chris is a short form of various names including Christopher, Christian, Christina, and Christine. Chris is also used as a name in its own right, but it is not as common.

chrissie.meaning_en: Chrissie is a feminine given name.

christa.meaning_en: Christa is a female given name, a diminutive of Christine. Notable people with the name include: Christa Ackroyd, British television and radio presenter Christa B.
christa.meaning_fr: Christa et Krista sont des variantes du prénom féminin Christiane .

christal.meaning_en: Christal is a feminine given name. Notable people with the name include: Christal Bezerra, Brazilian artistic gymnast Christal Clashing, Antiguan swimmer Christal Henner, American bridge player Christal Lloyd, American politician

christel.meaning_en: Christel is a given name of German origin.

christene.meaning_en: Christene is a feminine given name.

christi.meaning_en: Christi is a feminine given name.

christia.meaning_en: Christia is a given name. Notable people with the name include: Christia Adair Christia Brown Christia Mercer, American professor of philosophy at Columbia University Christia Sylf, French writer Christia Visser, South African actress and singer

christiaan.meaning_en: Christiaan is a Dutch, Flemish, and Afrikaans male given name. An archaic spelling of the name was Christiaen with "ae" to indicate the long sound "a".

christian.meaning_en: Christian is a unisex given name, which originated as a baptismal name used by persons of the Christian religion. It has been used as a given name since the Middle Ages.

christiana.meaning_en: Christiana or Christianna is a feminine given name.

christiane.meaning_en: Christiane or Christianne is a given name, derived from the Latin Christiana, the feminine form of Christianus. It can also be a Latinized version of Middle English Christin 'Christian'.
christiane.meaning_fr: Christiane est un prénom féminin d'origine latine. Ce prénom est inspiré du terme latin Christus qui signifie « Christ ». Il est fêté le 15 décembre ou le 14 janvier en l'honneur de Nino de Géorgie.

christien.meaning_en: Christien is a unisex given name. Notable people with the name include: Christien Anholt, English stage, television and film actor Christien Tinsley, make-up artist

famous.name: Maria Christina of the Two Sicilies

christina.meaning_en: Christina or Cristina is a feminine given name. It is a simplified form of the Latin Christiana, and a feminine form of Christianus or a Latinized form of the Middle English Christin 'Christian'. Short forms include Chris and Tina.

christine.meaning_en: Christine is feminine given name of Greek origin.

christoffer.meaning_en: Christopher is the English version of a Europe-wide name derived from the Greek name Χριστόφορος. The constituent parts are Χριστός, "Christ" or "Anointed", and φέρειν, "to bear"; hence the "Christ-bearer". As a given name, 'Christopher' has been in use since the 10th century.

christoph.meaning_en: Christoph is a male given name and surname. It is a German variant of Christopher.

christophe.meaning_en: Christophe is a male given name and a surname. It is a French variant of Christopher.

christopher.meaning_en: Christopher is the English version of a Europe-wide name derived from the Greek name Χριστόφορος. The constituent parts are Χριστός, "Christ" or "Anointed", and φέρειν, "to bear"; hence the "Christ-bearer". As a given name, 'Christopher' has been in use since the 10th century.

christos.meaning_en: Christos is a common Greek given name, which may be spelled as Christos, Chrestos, Chreistos, Christus, Chrestus, and Chreistus, Nicknames include Chris, Chrissie, Chrissy, Chreissie, Chreissy, Chreis, Essie, Eissie, Tos, Tossie, and Issie

christy.meaning_en: Christie or Christy is a given name, used in English for females. The name Christie originated from Italy in 1222, and derives from the Greek names Christos and Christiana. The name Christy appears in Ireland in 1345, and is a common masculine name there.

chucky.meaning_en: Chucky is an English masculine given name that is a diminutive form of Charles. Notable people known by this name include the following:

chyna.meaning_en: Chynna, Chyna, or Chynah can be both a given name and surname.

cian.meaning_en: Cian is a Gaelic given name meaning "ancient". Cian was the eighth most popular Irish boy's name in Ireland in 2003, and the fourteenth most popular in 2015. Anglicisations of Cian include Kian or Kyan.

ciara.meaning_en: Ciara is a popular Irish language female name and was tenth on the list of most popular names given to baby girls in Ireland in 2006.

ciaran.meaning_en: Ciarán or Ciaran is a traditionally male given name of Irish and Scottish origin. It means "little dark one" or "little dark-haired one", produced by appending a diminutive suffix to ciar. It is the masculine version of the name Ciara.
ciaran.meaning_fr: Cette page est la page d'homonymie de Ciarán et Ciaran. Ciarán est un prénom irlandais.

cicely.meaning_en: Cecilia is a personal name originating in the name of Saint Cecilia, the patron saint of music.

cicero.meaning_en: Cícero is a Portuguese masculine given name, mainly found in Brazil.

cillian.meaning_en: Killian or Kilian, as a given name, is an Anglicized version of the Irish name Cillian. The name Cillian was borne by several early Irish saints including missionaries to Artois and Franconia and the author of the life of St Brigid.

cinderella.meaning_en: Cinderella is a feminine given name. It was first used as the English name of a fairytale character but is now a given name in its own right.

cindi.meaning_en: Cindy is a feminine given name. Originally diminutive of Cynthia, Lucinda or Cinderella, it is also commonly used as a name on its own right. The name can also be spelled as Cindee, Cyndee, Syndee, Sindee, Sindi, Syndi, Syndy, Cindi, Cyndi, Cyndy, and Sindy.

cindy.meaning_en: Cindy is a feminine given name. Originally diminutive of Cynthia, Lucinda or Cinderella, it is also commonly used as a name on its own right. The name can also be spelled as Cindee, Cyndee, Syndee, Sindee, Sindi, Syndi, Syndy, Cindi, Cyndi, Cyndy, and Sindy.

cinthia.meaning_en: Cynthia is a feminine given name. It is often thought to be of Greek origin, but words and names with "inth" are actually Pre-Greek names belonging to another language family, before the Indo-European migrations. The name has been in use in the Anglosphere since the 17th century.

cipriano.meaning_en: Cipriano is a masculine given name. Notable people with the name include:

ciro.meaning_en: Ciro is an Italian and Spanish given name related to Cyrus.

clair.meaning_en: Claire or Clair is a given name of French origin. The word means clear in French in its feminine form.

claire.meaning_en: Claire or Clair is a given name of French origin. The word means clear in French in its feminine form.
claire.meaning_fr: Claire est un nom propre utilisé comme prénom, patronyme ou toponyme. D'origine latine, il dérive de l'adjectif clarus, qui donne au féminin clara, signifiant éclatant, brillant, mais également renommé, célèbre.

clara.meaning_en: Clara or Klara is a given name. It is the feminine form of the Late Latin name Clarus which meant "clear, bright, famous".
clara.meaning_fr: Clara est un prénom féminin qui se fête le 11 août. Prénom dérivé de Claire , du latin clarus, clara, clarum qui signifie claire, glorieux, brillant.

clare.meaning_en: Clare is a given name, the medieval English form of Clara. The related name Clair was traditionally considered male, but Clare and Claire are usually female. It is very often associated with the Irish County Clare.

clarence.meaning_en: Clarence is a masculine given name. It was adopted as a first name from the title of Albert Victor, Duke of Clarence, who was the eldest son of Edward VII.

clarice.meaning_en: Clarice is a female given name, an anglicization of the French Clarisse, derived from the Latin and Italian name Clarissa, which ultimately derives from clara. It can also be a female form of the male name Clarence. It may refer to:

clarissa.meaning_en: Clarissa is a female given name borrowed from Latin, Italian, and Portuguese,. It is a combination of St. Clare of Assisi's Latin name Clara and the suffix -issa, equivalent to -ess. Clarice is an anglicization of Clarisse, the French form of the same name.

clarisse.meaning_en: Clarisse is a female given name borrowed from French, derived from the Italian and Latin name Clarissa, originally denoting a nun of the Roman Catholic Order of St. Clare. It is a combination of St. Clare of Assisi's Latin name Clara and the suffix -issa, equivalent to -ess.

clark.meaning_en: Clark or Clarke is a given name, a transferred use of the English occupational surname derived from the Latin word clericus, meaning clerk. The name has been in use as a given name in the Anglosphere since the 1600s.

clarke.meaning_en: Clarke is a given name that originated as a transferred use of the surname Clarke. It has been used as a given name since the 1600s. The names Clark and Clarke, along with their spelling variations, have been influenced by well-known figures such as Clark Gable.

claud.meaning_en: Claud is a given name. Notable people with the name include: Claud Allister, English actor Claud Beelman, American architect Claud Irvine Boswell, Scottish judge Claud Thomas Bourchier, English recipient of the Victoria Cross Claud E.

famous.name: Claude Henri de Rouvroy, comte de Saint-Simon

claude.meaning_en: Claude is a French given name originating from the Latin name Claudius meaning "crippled" or "lame". In French, it is used for both men and women. In English, it is mostly used for men; it is an uncommon given name for women or a family name.

claudia.meaning_en: Claudia is a female given name equivalent to Claudius or Claudio. In Portuguese, it is accented Cláudia. A variant and cognate form is Klaudia. It was originally used to refer to any woman who belonged to the ancient Roman Claudia gens.

famous.name: Stéphanie, Grand Duchess Consort of Luxembourg

claudine.meaning_en: Claudine is a given name of French origin. It is the feminine form of the ancient Roman name Claudius. In the United States, the name was considered on the verge of extinction by 2013.

claudio.meaning_en: Claudio is an Italian and Spanish first name. In Portuguese, it is accented Cláudio. In Catalan and Occitan, it is Claudi, while in Romanian it is Claudiu.

clelia.meaning_en: Clelia is a feminine given name derived from the Latin Cloelia, associated with the root of the verb cluere "to have renown, fame," and the name therefore means "illustrious, famous." In Roman legend Cloelia was a maiden who was given to an Etruscan invader as a hostage, but managed to escape by swimming across the Tiber.
clelia.meaning_fr: Clélia est un prénom féminin d'origine Italienne, popularisé en France par le roman de Stendhal La Chartreuse de Parme.

clemence.meaning_fr: Clémence est un prénom féminin d'origine latine, dérivé de l'adjectif clemens, clementis qui signifie « bon », « indulgent », « doux ». Sa forme masculine est Clément.

clemente.meaning_en: Clemente is both an Italian, Spanish and French surname and a given name. Notable people with the surname include:

clementina.meaning_en: Clementina is a feminine given name.

famous.name: Clémentine of Orléans, Princess of Koháry

clementine.meaning_en: Clémentine or Clementine is a French feminine form of Clement. The name has been in use in English-speaking countries since the 19th century.

cleo.meaning_en: Cleo is a given name, derived from the name Clio in Greek mythology. As a spelling variant of Clio, the name is etymologically derived from the Greek root κλέω/κλείω, Latinised as kleos.

famous.name: Cleopatra Selene of Egypt and Syria

cleophas.meaning_en: Cleophas or Cléophas is a masculine given name, and a variant spelling of Cleopas, a figure of early Christianity.

cleophus.meaning_en: Cleophus is a masculine given name. Notable people with the name include:

cleveland.meaning_en: Cleveland is a masculine given name borne by: Cleveland Abbe, American meteorologist and advocate of time zones Cleveland Abbott, African-American football player, college football and basketball head coach and educator Cleveland Amory, American animal rights activist and author Cleveland Bailey, Jamaican cricketer Cleveland M.

clifton.meaning_en: Clifton is a given name. Notable people with the name include: Clifton Abraham, American and Canadian football player Clifton Bailey, Jamaican reggae musician, better known as Capleton Clifton Bloomfield, American serial killer Clifton R.

clinton.meaning_en: Clinton is a given name. It may be shortened informally to Clint.

clive.meaning_en: Clive is a name. People and fictional characters with the name include:

clodagh.meaning_en: Clodagh is a female given name of Irish origin. Lady Clodagh Anson, daughter of John Beresford, 5th Marquess of Waterford, was named after the River Clodiagh, which flows through the Marquess's estate at Curraghmore at County Waterford.

cloe.meaning_en: Chloe, also spelled Chloë, Chlöe, or Chloé, is a feminine name meaning "blooming" or "fertility" in Greek. The name ultimately derives, through Greek, from the Proto-Indo-European root *ǵʰelh₃-, which relates to the colors yellow and green.

clotaire.meaning_en: Chlothar is a Germanic given name, attested in Old English as Hloþhere, in Old High German as Lothari, and reconstructed in Frankish as *Hlodhari. It means "famous warrior", as a combination of the Germanic root hlut- and the word heri.

clothilde.meaning_fr: Clotilde ou Clothilde est un prénom féminin français. Il est fêté le 4 juin.

famous.name: Clémentine of Orléans, Princess of Koháry

clotilde.meaning_fr: Clotilde ou Clothilde est un prénom féminin français. Il est fêté le 4 juin.

clover.meaning_en: Clover is a modern given name derived from the common name for the plant, which was ultimately derived from the Old English word clāfre. The name has associations with Ireland and with good fortune due to traditional tales about the Irish shamrock or four-leaf clover.

clovis.meaning_en: Clovis is the modern conventional French form of the Old Frankish name ᚺᛚᛟᛞᛟᚹᛁᚷ or *"Hlōdowik" or "Hlōdowig", equivalent to the modern forms Louis, Lodewijk, Lewis, and Ludwig.
clovis.meaning_fr: Louis est un prénom masculin français, d'origine germanique.

clyde.meaning_fr: Clyde est un prénom écossais, sans doute tiré du fleuve Clyde coulant à Glasgow, sur la côte ouest de l'Écosse. Il tire son nom des collines rougeâtres de Glasgow. L'équivalent en hawaïen est Omea, qui signifie aussi une personne aimée et respectée.

codi.meaning_en: Cody is a name in the English language, ultimately of Irish origin. Spellings include Codi, Codie, Coedee, Kodi, Kodie, and Kody. Other variants are Coady and Codey.

codie.meaning_en: Cody is a name in the English language, ultimately of Irish origin. Spellings include Codi, Codie, Coedee, Kodi, Kodie, and Kody. Other variants are Coady and Codey.

cody.meaning_en: Cody is a name in the English language, ultimately of Irish origin. Spellings include Codi, Codie, Coedee, Kodi, Kodie, and Kody. Other variants are Coady and Codey.

cohen.meaning_en: Cohen is a masculine given name of Hebrew origin. It derives from the surname of the same spelling, meaning "priest." Cohen is a title associated with hereditary priests, most of whom descended from Aaron, the brother of Moses.

colby.meaning_en: Colby is a gender-neutral given name, meaning "coal town" or "Koli's town".

cole.meaning_en: Cole is a given name of English origin, originally used as an English surname. It is of Middle English origin, and its meaning is "swarthy, coal-black, charcoal".

colette.meaning_en: Colette is a French feminine given name.

coley.meaning_en: Coley is a unisex given name. Notable people with the name include:

colin.meaning_en: Colin is an English-language masculine given name. It has two distinct origins: A diminutive form of "Colle", itself an Old French short form of the name Nicolas. This name, but not the anglicized Gaelic name, is also found in the spelling Collin.

coline.meaning_fr: Coline est un prénom féminin issu du prénom Nicolas. Son équivalent masculin est Colin .

colleen.meaning_en: Colleen is an English-language name of Irish origin. It derives from the Irish word cailín "girl/woman", the diminutive of caile "woman, countrywoman".

collins.meaning_en: Collins is a given name, a transferred use of the English surname, Collins, which is ultimately derived from multiple sources.

colm.meaning_en: Colm is a masculine given name of Irish origin. It is not an Irish version of Colin, but like Callum and Malcolm derives from a Gaelic variation on columba, the Latin word for "dove".

colton.meaning_en: Colton is a masculine given name, meaning "coal town", "Cola's town", or "dark town". Prominent individuals with this name include:

concetta.meaning_en: Concetta is an Italian female given name.

concha.meaning_en: Concha is a Spanish surname of Latin origin. It was derived from the Latin word concha which means shell and is used as a topographic surname referring to those living in or near a cavity.

conner.meaning_en: Connor is an Irish male given name, anglicised from the compound Irish word Conchobhar, meaning "lover of hounds", or "lover of wolves".

connie.meaning_en: Connie is a given name. It is often a pet form of Concetta, Constance, Cornelia, Cornelius, Conor, Conrad, Constanza, Concepcion/Conception, Consuela, Consuelo, or Conner.

connor.meaning_en: Connor is an Irish male given name, anglicised from the compound Irish word Conchobhar, meaning "lover of hounds", or "lover of wolves".

conor.meaning_en: Conor is a male given name of Irish origin. The meaning of the name is "Lover of Wolves" or "Lover of Hounds". Conchobhar/Conchubhar or from the name Conaire, found in Irish legend as the name of the high king Conaire Mór and other heroes.

constance.meaning_en: Constance is a primarily feminine given name in use since the Middle Ages that is derived either from Constantia, a Late Latin name, or from the term meaning steadfast. In medieval England, diminutives of the name included Cust or Cussot.

constantin.meaning_en: Constantin is an Aromanian, Megleno-Romanian and Romanian male given name. It can also be a surname. For a list of notable people called Constantin, see Constantine.

constantinos.meaning_en: Constantine is a masculine and feminine given name and surname which is derived from the Latin name Constantinus, a hypocoristic of the first names Constans and Constantius, both meaning "constant, steadfast" in Latin.

famous.name: Constance of Castile, Duchess of Lancaster

consuelo.meaning_en: Consuelo is a female given name meaning "solace" or "consolation" in Spanish.

conway.meaning_en: Conway is a Welsh, Irish, and Scottish given name, the origin of which is unclear. It may originally have been an Anglicization of Welsh Conwy; of Irish Conbhuidhe or O Connmhachain; or of Scottish Gaelic Mac Conmheadha or Mac Connmhaigh.

cooper.meaning_en: Cooper is a masculine given name of English origin. Its meaning is “barrel maker”.

cora.meaning_en: Cora is a given name with multiple origins. It was used by James Fenimore Cooper for a character in his 1826 novel The Last of the Mohicans. It is today most commonly viewed as a variant name derived from the Ancient Greek Κόρη, an epithet of the Greek goddess Persephone.
cora.meaning_fr: Cora est un prénom féminin, principalement fêté le 18 mai avec saint Dioscore.

coral.meaning_en: Coral is a feminine given name derived from the precious coral used to make jewelry. The name is ultimately derived from the Greek word korallion and the Latin coralium. The name came into fashion in the Anglosphere in the late 1800s along with other gemstone names for girls.

coralee.meaning_en: Coralee is a feminine given name. Notable people with the name include: Coralee Oakes, Canadian politician Coralee O'Rourke, Australian politician Coralee Elliott Testar, Vancouver based producer and screenwriter

coralie.meaning_en: Coralie is a French female given name meaning "coral", derived from the Latin word coralium. It was the eighth most popular name for baby girls in Quebec in 2007.

coraline.meaning_en: Coraline is a feminine given name, usually considered a French diminutive of the name Coral, which is derived from the name for the precious coral used to make jewelry. It was first used by French composer Adolphe Adam for a character in his 1849 comic opera Le toréador.

corbin.meaning_en: Corbin is a masculine given name.

cordelia.meaning_en: Cordelia is a feminine given name. It was borne by the tragic heroine of Shakespeare's King Lear, a character based on the legendary queen Cordelia. The name is of uncertain origin.

coreen.meaning_en: Corina is a female given name of ancient Greek origin, derived from κόρη meaning "girl, maiden". Variants and diminutives include Corinna, Cori, Corri, Corinne, Corine, Kora, Korina and Korinna. Notable people with the name Coreen, Corina or Corine include:

corentin.meaning_fr: Corentin est un nom propre utilisé comme prénom et comme nom de famille.

corentine.meaning_fr: Corentine est un prénom féminin, associé à la ville de Quimper[réf. nécessaire] et dérivé de Corentin. D'origine celte, francisation de "Kaourentina", dérivé de "karent" qui signifie "amie". On le fête le 12 décembre. Il reste assez rare.

corin.meaning_en: Corin is a given name in English deriving from the Latin Quirinus, a Roman god. The meaning is unclear but is probably associated with "spear". It is used as a masculine or feminine given name, and also as a surname.

corina.meaning_en: Corina is a female given name of ancient Greek origin, derived from κόρη meaning "girl, maiden". Variants and diminutives include Corinna, Cori, Corri, Corinne, Corine, Kora, Korina and Korinna. Notable people with the name Coreen, Corina or Corine include:

corine.meaning_en: Corina is a female given name of ancient Greek origin, derived from κόρη meaning "girl, maiden". Variants and diminutives include Corinna, Cori, Corri, Corinne, Corine, Kora, Korina and Korinna. Notable people with the name Coreen, Corina or Corine include:

corinna.meaning_en: Corinna or Korinna is a female given name of ancient Greek origin, derived from κόρη meaning "girl, maiden". Notably, the ancient Greek lyric poet, as well as its use by Ovid for the women he addresses in the Amores, may have both infused the name's popularity.

corinne.meaning_en: Corinne is a female name, the French and English variant of Corina, of ancient Greek origin, derived from κόρη meaning "beautiful maiden". It became popular following the publication of Corinne, or Italy, an 1808 novel by Madame de Staël.

cormac.meaning_en: Cormac is a masculine given name in the Irish and English languages. The name is ancient in the Irish language and is also seen in the rendered Old Norse as Kormákr. Mac is Irish for "son", and can be used as either a prefix or a suffix. The derivation of "cor" is not so clear.

cornelius.meaning_en: Cornelius is an originally Roman masculine name. Its derivation is uncertain but is suspected to be from the Latin cornu, "horn". In Ireland it was used as an anglicization of the name Connor.

cosette.meaning_en: Cosette is a fictional character in the 1862 novel Les Misérables by Victor Hugo and in the many adaptations of the story for stage, film, and television. Her birth name, Euphrasie, is only mentioned briefly.

cosima.meaning_en: Cosima is a feminine given name, the feminine version of the name Cosimo. It is derived from the Greek Κοσμᾶς, meaning 'order', 'decency'. Cosmo was a fourth-century saint who was martyred with his brother Damian. They are the patron saints of medical doctors.

curtiss.meaning_en: Curtis or Curtiss is a common English given name and surname of Anglo-Norman origin, deriving from the Old French curteis which was in turn derived from Latin cohors. Nicknames include Curt, Curty and Curtie. The name means "polite, courteous, or well-bred".

cyndi.meaning_en: Cindy is a feminine given name. Originally diminutive of Cynthia, Lucinda or Cinderella, it is also commonly used as a name on its own right. The name can also be spelled as Cindee, Cyndee, Syndee, Sindee, Sindi, Syndi, Syndy, Cindi, Cyndi, Cyndy, and Sindy.

cynthia.meaning_en: Cynthia is a feminine given name. It is often thought to be of Greek origin, but words and names with "inth" are actually Pre-Greek names belonging to another language family, before the Indo-European migrations. The name has been in use in the Anglosphere since the 17th century.

cyril.meaning_en: Cyril is a masculine given name. It is derived from the Greek name Κύριλλος, meaning 'lordly, masterful', which in turn derives from Greek κυριος 'lord'.

cyrus.meaning_en: Cyrus is a Persian-language masculine given name. It is historically best known as the name of several Persian kings, most notably including Cyrus the Great, who founded the Achaemenid Empire in 550 BC.

dakota.meaning_en: Dakota is a unisex given name derived from the name of the Native American Dakota people. The name is translated to mean "friend", "friendly" or "allies" in the Yankton-Yanktonai and Santee dialects of the Dakota language.
dakota.meaning_fr: Dakota est un prénom épicène faussement considéré comme d'origine nord-amérindienne. Il signifierait « ami » en langue Sioux selon des livres américains de prénoms. Dakota est en réalité le nom d'une tribu Sioux, mais en aucun cas un prénom Sioux.

dalene.meaning_en: Dalene is a female given name. Notable people with the name include: Dalene Kurtis, Playboy model Dalene Matthee, South African author Dalene Stangl, American statistician Dalene Young, screenwriter for 1980 teen comedy-drama film Little Darlings

dorcas.meaning_en: Dorcas is a female given name. It derives from Dorcas, a figure from Acts of the Apostles in the New Testament.

doreen.meaning_en: Doreen, also occasionally spelt Dorean or Dorine, is a feminine given name, usually found in English-speaking countries. It is a combination of Dora with the suffix -een, which is related to the -ín suffix used in Irish, usually signifying small size or as an endearment.

dorian.meaning_en: Dorian is a given name of Greek origin. In Greek, the meaning of the name Dorian is of Doris, a district of Ancient Greece, or of Dorus, a legendary Greek hero. Dorus was a son of Hellen, the eponymous progenitor of the Hellenes.

douglas.meaning_en: Douglas is a masculine given name which originated from the surname Douglas. Although today the name is almost exclusively given to boys, it was used as a girl's name in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries in the north of England.
