maura.meaning_en: Maura is a female given name primarily used in English, Spanish, Italian, Greek, Scots Gaelic, and Irish. In Romance languages it appears as the feminine form of the Roman given name Maurus. In Gaelic languages it may be an Anglicisation of Máire, the Irish form of Mary.

maureen.meaning_en: Maureen is a female name. In Gaelic, it is Máirín, a pet form of Máire, which is derived from the Hebrew Miriam. Some notable bearers of the name are:
maureen.meaning_fr: Maureen est un prénom féminin qui peut évoquer : Maureen, chanteuse française Maureen Connolly, joueuse américaine de tennis Maureen Dor, actrice et chanteuse belge Maureen Dunlop de Popp, pilote anglaise et argentine Maureen Forrester, chanteuse canadienne Maureen Constance Guinness, personnalité de la société mondaine anglaise et irlandaise Maureen Jelagat, athlète kényane Maureen Kaila Vergara, coureuse cycliste américaine Maureen F.

maurice.meaning_en: Maurice is a traditionally masculine given name, also used as a surname. It originates as a French name derived from the Latin Mauritius or Mauricius and was subsequently used in other languages. Its popularity is due to Mauritius, a saint of the Theban Legion.

mauricette.meaning_fr: Mauricette est un prénom féminin dérivé du prénom masculin Maurice. Les Mauricette sont fêtées le 22 septembre. Pour voir toutes les pages commençant par Mauricette, consulter la liste générée automatiquement pour le prénom Mauricette.

mauricio.meaning_en: Mauricio is a Spanish and Portuguese masculine given name, equivalent to English Maurice and derived from the Roman Mauritius. It is of Latin origin, and its meaning is "dark-skinned, Moorish".

maurille.meaning_en: Maurilio or Maurelio, Maurille and Maurílio are variations of the Latin name Maurilius.

maurizio.meaning_en: Maurizio is an Italian masculine given name, derived from the Roman name Mauritius. Mauritius is a derivative of Maurus, meaning dark-skinned, Moorish.

maury.meaning_en: Maury or Maurey is a given name, often a short form of Maurice. Notable people with the name include: Maury Allen, American sportswriter Maury Bray, American football player Maury Buford, retired National Football League punter Maury Chaykin, Canadian-American actor Maury M.

mavis.meaning_en: Mavis is a feminine given name, derived from a name for the common Old World song thrush. Its first modern usage was in Marie Corelli's 1895 novel The Sorrows of Satan, which featured a character named Mavis Clare.

maxine.meaning_en: Maxine is an English feminine given name created as a feminine version of the name Max. It has been in regular use since the 1880s. Other names with the diminutive suffix -een, -ene, or -ine were also in fashion during the late 19th century and early 20th century.

maxwell.meaning_en: Maxwell is a masculine given name. It is of English and Scottish origin, meaning "From Mack's Spring". The name originates as a place name from a location on the River Tweed in Scotland and first recorded in 1144 CE, spelled Mackeswell.

may.meaning_en: May is an English feminine given name. It is derived from the name of the month, which comes from Maia, the name of a Roman fertility goddess. It can also be a variant of the Arabic name Mai مي, which either means water or little gazelle.

maya.meaning_en: Maya is a feminine name in various languages with various meanings. In the ancient Indian language Sanskrit, Māyā means "the illusory nature of reality or the illusion of creation", and is an alternate name of the Hindu goddess Lakshmi.

mayme.meaning_en: Mayme is a female given name. People with the name include: Mayme Agnew Clayton, librarian and leader of the Western States Black Research and Education Center Mayme Cox, née Harding, first wife of politician James M.

mayola.meaning_en: The name Mayola, a variant of the name 'May', is a female name which means 'born in the month of May'. The name 'May' derives from Maia, the name of a Roman goddess. The name could also refer to hawthorn flower that blossoms in the month of May.

mayra.meaning_en: Mayra or Mäyrä is a given name.

maysie.meaning_en: Maisie, also spelt Maisy or other minor variations, is a feminine given name. It is a pet form of the Scottish Gaelic name Mairead or the Irish name Mairéad, which are the equivalent of the English name Margaret.

mayte.meaning_en: Maite also spelled Mayté, Maytee, Maytte or Maïté, is a female given name of Iberian origin popular throughout the Hispanic world and Brazil. The name is the Basque word for "love", though it can also be a nickname for "María Teresa" and "María Esther".

maelys.meaning_en: Maëlys is a French feminine name of Breton origin. It is a feminine form of the name Maël, meaning "chief" or "prince". The name Maël was popularized by a fifth-century Breton saint Maël.
maelys.meaning_fr: Maëlys est un prénom d'origine bretonne. Il est dérivé de Mael qui signifie « prince ». Il apparaît en France dans les années 1980 et devient courant dans les années 2000. Depuis 2008, il figure dans les quinze prénoms les plus donnés au niveau national[réf. nécessaire].

meng.meaning_en: Meng is a Chinese surname. Meng is a shi surname or clan name, as opposed to the xing category of surname, ancestral name.

menno.meaning_en: Menno is a Dutch masculine given name of Old Frisian origin. It was made popular by the influential Frisian religious reformer Menno Simons, and the name was spread by his followers, the Mennonites. Menno is the Dutch version of Frisian Meine.

mercedes.meaning_en: Mercedes is a Spanish female name, popularized in the form of María de las Mercedes, which is one of the Roman Catholic titles of the Virgin Mary.
mercedes.meaning_fr: Mercedes est un prénom féminin espagnol. La forme Mercédès existe aussi en français.

meredith.meaning_en: Meredith is a Welsh given name, and a surname common in parts of Wales. As a personal name, it was historically usually given to boys, but it has more recently been given mainly to girls, especially outside Wales.
meredith.meaning_fr: Meredith est un prénom rare, et un nom de famille fréquent dans certaines régions du Pays de Galles. Il provient du gallois Maredudd, signifiant « grand seigneur ».

meriem.meaning_en: Meryem is a feminine Turkish given name. It is the Turkish form of Maryam, and is the name used in Turkey to refer to Mary, the mother of Jesus. Meriem is another variant form, found as a given name and surname of North African origin.

merissa.meaning_en: Marissa is a feminine given name typically used in Western culture. It is a variation of Maris, which is Latin for 'of the sea'. It can also be spelled Marrisa, Merissa or Marisa. Marissa also means "little Mary" referring to the Virgin Mary.

micah.meaning_en: Micah is a given name. Micah is the name of several people in the Tanakh, and means "Who is like God?”. The name is sometimes found with theophoric extensions. Suffix theophory in Yah and in Yahweh results in Michaiah or Michaihu, meaning who is like Yahweh?

michael.meaning_en: Michael is a common masculine given name usually thought to be from the Hebrew rhetorical question מי כאל, "Who [is] like [the Hebrew god] El?", thus being a theophoric name whose answer is "there is none like El", or "there is none as famous and powerful as God." This question is known in Latin as Quis ut Deus?
michael.meaning_fr: Michael ou Michaël, parfois orthographié Mickael ou Mickaël, Mikael ou Mikaël, ou Micael ou encore Mikhael, est un prénom masculin issu de l'hébreu Mika'el, qui signifie « qui est semblable à Dieu ? ». Mickael tire ses origines des textes bibliques.

mir.meaning_en: Mir is a given name. In the majority of cases it is the name originated in the Indian subcontinent. It can also be a part of a two-part given name, such as Mir-Hasan or Mir-Fatah. A number of historical persons are commonly referred by the name starting with honorific "Mir".

mira.meaning_en: Mira is a feminine given name with varying meanings. In the Romance languages, it is related to the Latin word ''mirus'' for 'wonder' and 'wonderful'. In Slavic languages, it means 'peace' and is often used as part of a longer name, such as Miroslava, Mirjana, or Sławomira.

mirabel.meaning_en: Mirabel is a female name stemming from the Latin word mirabilis, meaning "wondrous" or "of wondrous beauty". It was used as both a male and female name in the Middle Ages, but is now almost exclusively female.

miran.meaning_en: Miran is a given name and surname. The name Miran is derived from the word Mir and the suffix 'an' which is a very common component of Slavic names.

miranda.meaning_en: Miranda is a feminine given name of Latin origin, meaning "worthy of admiration", deriving the feminine name from the Latin word mirandus.

miray.meaning_en: Miray is a Turkish female given name. According to the Turkish Language Institute Miray is a Turkish name created from the Persian root Mir and Turkish root Ay. Mir in Persian means leader and Ay in Turkish means the moon.

mireille.meaning_en: Mireille is a French given name, derived from the Provençal Occitan name Mirèio. It could be related to the Occitan verb mirar "to look, to admire" or to the given names Miriam "Myriam", Maria "Mary".

musa.meaning_en: Musa is an Arabic male name and cognate for "Moses".

musab.meaning_en: Mosab is a given name. Notable people with the given name include: Mosab Amrani, Moroccan-Dutch kickboxer Mosab Balhous, Syrian footballer Mosab Abu Toha, Palestinian writer, poet, scholar, and librarian Mosab Hassan Yousef, American author and former militant

muskan.meaning_en: Muskan is a given name, mostly feminine, found in Pakistan, India, Nepal, and Bangladesh.

mustafa.meaning_en: Mustafa is one of the names of the Islamic prophet Muhammad, and the name means "chosen, selected, appointed, preferred", used as an Arabic given name and surname. Mustafa is a common name in Muslim-majority countries.

mustapha.meaning_en: Mustafa is one of the names of the Islamic prophet Muhammad, and the name means "chosen, selected, appointed, preferred", used as an Arabic given name and surname. Mustafa is a common name in Muslim-majority countries.

mya.meaning_en: Mya is a primarily feminine given name of uncertain origins. One source considers it to be a 20th-century phonetic spelling of the name Maya or Mia, names that have multiple, different meanings and origins in different languages.

mychael.meaning_en: Mychael is a masculine given name. Notable people with the name include: Mychael Danna, Canadian composer Mychael Knight, American fashion designer Mychael Urban, American sportswriter, radio and TV personality

mykel.meaning_en: Mykel is a masculine given name.

mylene.meaning_en: Mylene or Mylène is a given name, a contraction of Marie-Hélène.
mylene.meaning_fr: Mylène est un prénom féminin, contraction de Marie et d'Hélène, surnom créé par Mylène Demongeot[réf. nécessaire]. Marie vient de l'hébreu mar-yâm et signifie « celle qui élève ». Hélène vient du grec helê et signifie « éclat du soleil ». Mylène est fêtée le 15 ou le 18 août.

myles.meaning_en: Myles is a masculine given name, a variant spelling of Miles.

myra.meaning_en: The name Myra was created by the 17th-century poet Fulke Greville 1st Barone Brooke.

myriam.meaning_en: Miriam is a feminine given name recorded in Biblical Hebrew in the Book of Exodus as the name of the sister of Moses, the prophetess Miriam. Spelling variants include French Myriam, German Mirjam, Mirijam; hypocoristic forms include Mira, Miri and Mimi.

myriane.meaning_en: Myriane is a French feminine given name. Notable people with the name include: Myriane Houplain, French politician Myriane Samson, Canadian figure skater

myron.meaning_en: Myron is a masculine given name used in English-speaking and Eastern European countries including Romania, Ukraine and Russia. Non-religious or Christianized Jews have used this name as a Gentile replacement of the Jewish name Meir.

meloe.meaning_fr: Méloé est un prénom féminin. Il a surtout été attribué en Charente-Maritime, puis en Louisiane et aux Antilles et est en évolution, 156 naissances depuis 1950 avec un fort taux en 2004 . Certains[Qui ?] disent que ce prénom serait un mélange de Mélanie et de Chloé.

nabil.meaning_en: Nabīl, Nabeel, or Nabyl, rendered in some languages as Nebil, is a masculine given name of Arabic origin, meaning "noble". The feminine version is Nabila, Nabilah, Nabeela or Nabeelah. Notable people with the name include:
nabil.meaning_fr: Nabil est un nom propre d'origine arabe qui signifie "noble".

nacer.meaning_fr: Nacer ou Nacir est un prénom arabe masculin, qui signifie vainqueur.

nada.meaning_en: Nada is a feminine given name found with the etymology of 'hope' in South Slavic-speaking countries of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Slovenia and Serbia, and the etymology of 'dew' in Arabic-speaking countries.

nadeem.meaning_en: NadeemIt means "best friend of the drinker", "companion", "confidant", or "friend". The name is common among many communities, including Christians, Muslims and Jews, in the Greater Middle East, the Balkans, and South Asia.

nadeen.meaning_en: Nadine is a female given name. It is a French elaboration of the name Nadia, itself being a pet form of the Ukrainian virtue name Nadia. It is also commonly used amongst Arabic communities and may mean in Arabic: نادين, romanized: nādīn, lit.

nadia.meaning_en: Nadia is a female name. Variations include Nadja, Nadya, Nadine, Nadiya, and Nadiia. Most variations of the name are derived from Arabic, Slavic languages, or both.
nadia.meaning_fr: Nadia ou Nadja est un nom propre, utilisé notamment comme prénom féminin. De même étymologie que Nadège ou Nadine, ce prénom se fête aux mêmes dates, le 25 mai en Occident et le 18 septembre en Orient.

nadim.meaning_en: NadeemIt means "best friend of the drinker", "companion", "confidant", or "friend". The name is common among many communities, including Christians, Muslims and Jews, in the Greater Middle East, the Balkans, and South Asia.

nadine.meaning_en: Nadine is a female given name. It is a French elaboration of the name Nadia, itself being a pet form of the Ukrainian virtue name Nadia. It is also commonly used amongst Arabic communities and may mean in Arabic: نادين, romanized: nādīn, lit.
nadine.meaning_fr: Le prénom Nadine est dérivé du prénom Nadia, lui-même venant du russe « nadejda » qui signifie « Espérance ». De même étymologie que Nadège ou Nadeen, il se fête aux mêmes dates, le 25 mai en Occident et le 18 septembre en Orient.

nadiya.meaning_en: Nadiya or Nadiia is a feminine given name, from a Ukrainian word meaning "hope".

nadja.meaning_en: Nadja is a female name, that is used predominantly throughout the Mediterranean region, and the Arab world. Its origins are in the Arabic languages. The Serbian and Montenegrin spelling is Nađa.

nael.meaning_fr: Naël est un prénom masculin popularisé dans le début des années 2000, porté par environ 7 000 personnes en France[Quand ?], et dont la tendance est en forte croissance. Ce prénom a plusieurs origines possibles.

nafisa.meaning_en: Nafisa or also spelled as Nafesa and Nafisah is an Arabic feminine given name meaning valuable, precious, extremely desired.
nafisa.meaning_fr: Nafisa ou Nafissa est un prénom féminin d'origine arabe qui s'est répandu dans le monde arabo-musulman. Parmi celle qui portent ou ont porté ce prénom : Nafisa al-Sayyida, érudite et sainte musulmane vénérée au Caire.

nafissa.meaning_en: Nafissa is a given name. Notable people with the name include: Nafissa Sid Cara, French politician Nafissa Souleymane, Nigerien sprinter Nafissa Thompson-Spires, American writer

nahla.meaning_en: Nahla is a feminine given name of Arabic origin. The name is of Arabic origin meaning "first drink of water" or "water in the desert", there's also Nahla valley in Iraq. Additionally, the latinized term Nahla can also refer to honeybee in Arabic.

naiara.meaning_en: Naiara is a feminine given name. Notable people with the name include: Naiara Azevedo, Brazilian singer-songwriter Naiara Beristain, Spanish football player Naiara Egozkue, Spanish handball player Naiara Moreno, Spanish singer Naiara Telletxea, Spanish road cyclist

nail.meaning_en: Nail is a masculine given name. In Turkish it refers to those who accomplish their goals and are conquerors.

naila.meaning_en: Naila or Na'ila is a female given name of Arabic origin meaning "gracious".
naila.meaning_fr: Naïla est un prénom féminin sémite, répandu en Afrique du Nord.

naiomi.meaning_en: Naiomi is a female given name. Notable people with the name include: Naiomi Cameron, American mathematician Naiomi Glasses, American textile artist and skateboarder

naira.meaning_en: Naira is a feminine given name. Notable people with the name include: Naira Gelashvili, Georgian writer Naira Hovakimyan, Armenian game theorist Naira Melkumian, Artsakhi politician Naira Beatriz Vier, Brazilian badminton player Naira Zohrabyan, Armenian politician

najat.meaning_en: Najat is an Arabic female given name meaning "savior" or "salvation". In some countries it can be spelled Nagat.
najat.meaning_fr: Najat est un prénom d'origine arabe signifiant « sauveur » ou « sauvetage ».

najwa.meaning_fr: Najwa ou Najoua ou Najoie est un prénom arabe féminin qui signifie « secret » ou « confidence ».

nakia.meaning_en: Nakia is an unisex given name of multiple origins and meanings. Arabic meaning: "pure". Not many baby naming sites point out other origins of the name. They also neglect to inform of any other pronunciation the name has.

nana.meaning_en: Nana is a given name that has different origins in several countries across the world. Its use as a feminine or masculine name varies culturally.

nancy.meaning_en: Nancy is a feminine English language given name. The name Nancy was originally a diminutive form of Annis, a medieval English vernacular form of Agnes. In some English dialects, "mine" was used instead of "my" and "Mine Ancy" eventually became Nancy.

nancye.meaning_en: Nancy is a feminine English language given name. The name Nancy was originally a diminutive form of Annis, a medieval English vernacular form of Agnes. In some English dialects, "mine" was used instead of "my" and "Mine Ancy" eventually became Nancy.

nao.meaning_en: Nao is a common feminine Japanese given name which is occasionally used by males. It is also a short name for Naoko, Naomi, Naoto, etc.

naoki.meaning_en: Naoki is a masculine Japanese given name and surname.

naomi.meaning_en: Naomi or Noemi is a given name of separate biblical Hebrew and Japanese origin used in various languages and cultures.

napoleon.meaning_en: Napoléon is the French form of the Italian given name Napoleone. Notable people with the name include:

narcisse.meaning_fr: Venant du latin Narcissus, lui-même emprunté au grec ancien Narkissos qui désigne la fleur narcisse, Narcisse est un nom propre utilisé comme prénom essentiellement masculin, parfois féminin, ou comme patronyme.

narek.meaning_en: Narek, or Nareg in Western Armenian, is an Armenian masculine given name, derived from the name of the village of Narek, where the famous 10th-century Armenian monk and poet Gregory of Narek lived and wrote his Book of Lamentations, commonly known as Narek.

naseem.meaning_fr: Nassim est un prénom d'origine arabe existant aussi sous la version féminine Nassima.

nashla.meaning_en: Nashla is a feminine given name of uncertain origins, primarily used among Spanish speakers in North America.

nasreen.meaning_en: Nasrin is a feminine given name in Persian, meaning "wild rose". It is among the most popular names given to girls born in Iran.

nasser.meaning_en: Nasser is a masculine given name, commonly found in Arabic. Alternative spellings of this name, possibly due to transliteration, include Naser, Nassar, Nasir, Naseer, or Nacer. People with this name may include:
nasser.meaning_fr: Nasser est un prénom arabe, seul ou composé en Abd el-Nasser, parfois un nom de famille, rendu célèbre par Gamal Abdel Nasser, second président de l'Égypte de 1956 à 1970.

nassim.meaning_fr: Nassim est un prénom d'origine arabe existant aussi sous la version féminine Nassima.

natale.meaning_en: Natale is a male given name.
natale.meaning_fr: Nathalie est un prénom féminin d'origine latine.

natalee.meaning_en: Natalee is a female given name. It is a variant of the name Natalie, though uncommon according to the U.S. Census Bureau.

natalia.meaning_en: Natalia is a female given name with the original Late Latin meaning of "Christmas Day". In Russian, a common diminutive is Natasha.
natalia.meaning_fr: Nathalie est un prénom féminin d'origine latine.

natalie.meaning_en: Natalie is a feminine given name derived from the Latin phrase natale domini, meaning "birth of the Lord". Further alternative spellings of the name include Nathalie, Natalee, and Natalia/Natalija.

natalina.meaning_en: Natalia is a female given name with the original Late Latin meaning of "Christmas Day". In Russian, a common diminutive is Natasha.
natalina.meaning_fr: Natalina est un prénom féminin écrit aussi Nataline, d'origine italienne et portugaise, variante de Nathalie.

nataliya.meaning_en: Nataliya or Natalya is the Ukrainian and Russian form of the female given name Natalia. The name Natasha, being originally a diminutive form of Natalya, became an independent name outside the Russian-speaking states since the late 1800s.
nataliya.meaning_fr: Natalya est un prénom féminin d'origine russe et ukrainienne, vient du prénom dérivé de Nathalie.

nataly.meaning_en: Nataly is a female given name, a variant form of Natalie.
nataly.meaning_fr: Nataly est un prénom féminin pouvant désigner:

natascha.meaning_en: Natasha is a name of Russian origin. It is the diminutive form of the Latin name Natalia.

natasha.meaning_en: Natasha is a name of Russian origin. It is the diminutive form of the Latin name Natalia.

natashia.meaning_en: Natashia is a given name. Notable people with the name include: Natashia Boland, Australian mathematician Natashia Deón, American novelist, attorney, and activist Natashia Holmes, American politician Natashia Williams, American actress

nate.meaning_en: Nate is a given name, frequently used as a diminutive of Nathan, Nathanael or Nathaniel.

nathalia.meaning_fr: Nathalia est un prénom féminin, variante de Nathalie.

nathalie.meaning_en: Nathalie is a female given name. It is a variant of the name Natalie/Natalia which is found in many languages, and is especially common in French and English-speaking countries.
nathalie.meaning_fr: Nathalie est un prénom féminin d'origine latine.

nathaly.meaning_en: Natalie is a feminine given name derived from the Latin phrase natale domini, meaning "birth of the Lord". Further alternative spellings of the name include Nathalie, Natalee, and Natalia/Natalija.

nathan.meaning_en: Nathan is a masculine given name. It is derived from the Hebrew verb נָתָן‎ meaning gave.

nathanial.meaning_en: Nathanael is an English name of Hebrew origin. It is of Biblical origin and holds significance for Jews and Christians. Several figures in both the Old and New Testament bear the name.

nathaniel.meaning_en: Nathaniel is an English variant of the biblical Hebrew name Nathanael. It can be a given or surname.

nava.meaning_en: Nava is a female given name.

naveen.meaning_en: Naveen or Navin is an Indian male given name and surname. The word means "new", "young", "bright", "creative". Naveen is chiefly used in Indian languages, and its origin is Sanskrit. It is derived from the element 'Navina' meaning new.

nayeli.meaning_en: Nayeli is a feminine given name of Zapotec origin of uncertain meaning. It has been used primarily in the Hispanic community in the United States as well as in Mexico. The name has been among the one thousand most used names for girls in the United States since 1993.

nayla.meaning_fr: Nayla est le prénom de Nayla Moawad, née en 1940 : femme politique libanaise Nayla Farouki professeure et essayiste française d'origine libanaise. Nayla, un personnage fictif de l'univers de Dune.

nazar.meaning_en: Nazar is a masculine name with multiple origins.

naziha.meaning_en: Naziha is a feminine given name of Arabic origin. Notable people with the name include:

nazim.meaning_en: Nazim is an Arabic masculine given name. The pronunciation of the Arabic letter Ẓāʾ is often closer to a strong "d" sound; thus, the name's pronunciation differs based on the spoken varieties of Arabic and consequently in its transcription.

nazli.meaning_en: Nazlı is a common feminine Turkish given name. It means "delicate" or "gracious" in Turkish.

ndeye.meaning_en: Ndeye, Ndèye or N'deye is a Senegalese feminine given name. Notable people with the name include:

nechama.meaning_en: Nechama or Nehama is a Hebrew feminine given name literally meaning "consolation".

ned.meaning_en: Ned is an English given name and variant of Ed, sometimes short for Edward, Edmund, Edgar, or Edwin.

nedra.meaning_en: Nedra is a female given name.

neil.meaning_en: Neil is a masculine name of Irish origin. The name is an anglicisation of the Irish Niall which is of disputed derivation. The Irish name may be derived from words meaning "cloud", "passionate", "victory", "honour" or "champion".

neila.meaning_en: Neila is a feminine given name. Notable people with the name include: Neila Gonji, Tunisian politician Neila Sathyalingam, Singaporean classical Indian dancer, choreographer, and instructor

nela.meaning_en: Nela is a Croatian, Czech and Slovak feminine given name that serves as a diminutive form of Antonela and Antonie in Croatia, Czech Republic and Slovakia.

nelda.meaning_en: Nelda is a given name. Notable people with the name include: Nelda Garrone, Italian mezzo-soprano Nelda Martinez, American real estate agent and politician Nelda Speaks, American politician

nelia.meaning_en: Nelia is a feminine given name. It originated as a short form of Cornelia or Kornelia.

nell.meaning_en: Nell is a traditional nickname for Eleanor. Nell is the name of:

nello.meaning_en: Nello is an Italian masculine given name.

nelly.meaning_en: Nelly and Nellie are female given names, also used as nicknames, which are derived from the names Helen, Ellen, Petronella, Danielle, Cornelia, Eleanor, Janelle, Chanelle, Penelope, Elizabeth, Rachel, Natalie or Noelia.
nelly.meaning_fr: Nelly est un prénom emprunté à l'anglais, diminutif de Hélène, du grec Hếlê signifiant « chaleur », « splendeur du soleil » ou de Éléonore, du germanique Ali, « autre ou étranger » et -nord, « Nord ». Nelly est fêté le 18 août avec sainte Hélène.

nels.meaning_en: Nels is a given name. Notable people with the given name include: Nels Ackerson, American lawyer Nels N.

nelson.meaning_en: Nelson is an English, Scottish, Irish, Northern Irish, Scots-Irish, and Scandinavian given name, more commonly used as a surname. It is derived from a patronymic name created from the given name "Nell".

neri.meaning_en: Neri is a unisex given name mainly used in Israel. It is derived from Hebrew ner meaning candle. It is a variant form of Neriya, meaning "Yah is my candle".

nesrine.meaning_en: Nesrine is a given name. Notable people with the name include: Nesrine Ben Kahia, Tunisian table tennis player Nesrine Daoula, Tunisian handball player Nesrine Hamza, Tunisian handball player Nesrine Merouane, Algerian volleyball player

ness.meaning_en: Ness is a unisex given name, which means "from the headland".

nestor.meaning_en: Nestor, or Néstor, is a given name of Greek origin. In Greek mythology it comes from that of Nestor, the son of Neleus, the King of Pylos and Chloris. The Greek derivation is from a combination of νέομαι, néomai, 'go back', and νόστος, nóstos, 'one who returns from travels'.

netta.meaning_en: Netta is a short form of many names ending -netta, including Aquanetta, Arnetta, Dawnetta, Janetta and Jenetta, as part of the largest etymological root of names with over five hundred variations, both male and female.

nettie.meaning_en: Nettie is a feminine given name that is a diminutive form of Annette, Jeanette, Lynnette and Antonia. Its popularity in the United States has continually declined since its peak in the 1910s and 1920s. Notable people with this name include:

nevaeh.meaning_en: Nevaeh is a feminine given name which was coined by spelling heaven backwards. It peaked in popularity in the 2000s and 2010s but remains one of the most popular girls' names as of 2020.

nevan.meaning_en: Nevan was a saint in Irish folklore whose feast day was reputedly marked in mid-September. In Seathrún Céitinn's General History of Ireland, Naomhán is described as the "son of Maolciarain, primate of Ireland".

neven.meaning_en: Neven is a Slavic masculine given name, meaning Calendula officinalis in the Serbo-Croatian language. It is the masculine form of the feminine Slavic name, Nevena.

newton.meaning_en: Notable people with given name Newton include: Newton, stage name of Billy Myers, British firefighter turned pop singer Newton Araújo da Costa Júnior, Brazilian footballer Newton D. R. Allen, American politician Newton D.

nia.meaning_en: Nia is a given name which appears in many cultures. In Bulgaria, it is a short form of the feminine name Evgenia.

niall.meaning_en: Niall is a male given name of Irish origin. The original meaning of the name is unknown, but popular modern sources have suggested that it means "champion".
niall.meaning_fr: Niall est un mot gaélique signifiant champion[réf. nécessaire]. Niall est utilisé comme prénom et comme patronyme.

niamh.meaning_en: Niamh is an Irish feminine given name, anglicised as Neve, Nieve, Neave, Neavh or Neeve. In Irish mythology, Niamh is the daughter of the god of the sea, Manannán mac Lir and one of the queens of Tír na nÓg, the land of eternal youth. She was the lover of the poet-hero Oisín.

niara.meaning_en: Niara is a given name. Notable people with the given name include: Niara Bely, Luso-African queen and businesswoman Niara Scarlett, British singer-songwriter Niara Sudarkasa, American scholar, educator, Africanist and anthropologist

niccolo.meaning_en: Niccolò is an Italian male given name, derived from the Greek Nikolaos meaning "Victor of people" or "People's champion". There are several male variations of the name: Nicolò, Niccolò, Nicolas, and Nicola. The female equivalent is Nicole.

nichelle.meaning_en: Nichelle is a given name. Notable people with the name include: Nichelle Nichols, American actress, singer, and voice artist Nichelle Prince, Canadian soccer player Nichelle Tramble Spellman, American television producer and writer

nichola.meaning_en: Nicola or Nichola is a Latinised version of the Greek personal name Nikolaos, derived from the nikē meaning "victory", and laos meaning "people", therefore implying the meaning "victory of the people". Nicola is both a male and female name, depending on cultural norms.

famous.name: Louis Mountbatten, 1st Earl Mountbatten of Burma

nicholas.meaning_en: Nicholas is a male name, the Anglophone version of an ancient Greek name in use since antiquity, and cognate with the modern Greek Νικόλαος, Nikolaos. It originally derived from a combination of two Greek words meaning 'victory' and 'people'.

nicholaus.meaning_en: Nicholaus is a masculine given name.

nichole.meaning_en: Nichole is a feminine given name.

nicky.meaning_en: Nicky is a diminutive form of the name Nicholas, Nicola and Nicole, occasionally used as a given name in its own right. Sometimes it is spelled as Nikki, Niki. It can also be used as a diminutive of Dominic.

nicodemus.meaning_en: Nicodemus is a masculine given name of Greek origin meaning “victory of the people.” Nicodemus is a Biblical figure. Nikodem, a Croatian and Polish version of the name, was among the most popular names for newborn boys in Poland in 2022.

nicola.meaning_en: Nicola or Nichola is a Latinised version of the Greek personal name Nikolaos, derived from the nikē meaning "victory", and laos meaning "people", therefore implying the meaning "victory of the people". Nicola is both a male and female name, depending on cultural norms.

nicolas.meaning_fr: Nicolas est un prénom masculin d’étymologie grecque.

nicole.meaning_en: Nicole is a feminine given name and a surname. The given name Nicole is a French feminine derivative of the masculine given name Nicolas, which is ultimately from the Ancient Greek Νικόλαος, composed of the elements níkē “victory” and laós “people”. There are many variants.

nicoletta.meaning_en: Nicoletta is a name and feminine given name derived from the Greek Nikolaos, most often used in Italy, Sweden, Denmark and Norway. Nicoletta is also a surname. Notable people with the name include:

niels.meaning_en: Niels is a male given name, equivalent to Nicholas, which is common in Denmark, Belgium, Norway and the Netherlands. The Norwegian and Swedish variant is Nils. The name is a developed short form of Nicholas or Greek Nikolaos, after Saint Nicholas.

nieve.meaning_en: Niamh is an Irish feminine given name, anglicised as Neve, Nieve, Neave, Neavh or Neeve. In Irish mythology, Niamh is the daughter of the god of the sea, Manannán mac Lir and one of the queens of Tír na nÓg, the land of eternal youth. She was the lover of the poet-hero Oisín.

nigel.meaning_en: Nigel is an English masculine given name. The English Nigel is found in records dating from the Middle Ages; however, it was not used much before being revived by 19th-century antiquarians.
nigel.meaning_fr: Nigel est un prénom anglais. En anglais australien royale, c'est un terme familier pour un « homme socialement Supérieur » ou une personne avec pleins d'amis, provenant du nom étant rare dans les années 1980[style à revoir][pas clair].

nihad.meaning_en: Nihad is an Arabic masculine given name.

nika.meaning_en: Nika is a female or male given name having multiple origins in different languages and countries. In Slavic countries the name comes from the Ancient Greek goddess of victory "Nike".

nikhil.meaning_en: Nikhil is a male name of Sanskrit origin. It is predominantly found in India, Nepal, and the diaspora of these countries. The name means "complete" or "whole".

niki.meaning_en: Niki is a first given unisex name. Niki has a Persian origin and it is a female name, meaning kindness, Being good, good, benevolent, good turn, goodness, nobility, right; 2- comfort, prosperity, afterlife reward.

nikita.meaning_en: Nikita is a common masculine name in Eastern Europe and Greece. The Russian variant originated as a Greek name, and subsequently Russian name. The Ukrainian and Belarusian variants are Mykyta, and Mikita, respectively. The Romanian variant is Nichita.

nikki.meaning_en: Nikki is a given name. It is commonly a nickname for Nicholas and its variants Nikolina, Nicole, Nicola; and Nikita, and Veronica. It is also a Punjabi name meaning “little one”, with its male counterpart being Nikku.

niklaus.meaning_en: Niklaus is a masculine given name and surname. Niklaus comes from the Greek word nikolaos, meaning victory of the people. It’s a variant of the likewise Greek-origin given name Nicholas.

nikodem.meaning_en: Nikodem is a masculine given name. It is a variant of the given name Nicodemus.

nikola.meaning_en: Nikola is a given name which, like Nicholas, is a version of the Greek Nikolaos and it means "the winner of the people". It is common as a masculine given name in the South Slavic countries, while in West Slavic countries it is primarily found as a feminine given name.
nikola.meaning_fr: Nikola est un prénom qui, comme Nicolas, est une version du grec Nikolaos. Il est courant comme prénom masculin dans les pays slaves du Sud, tandis que dans les pays slaves occidentaux, on le trouve principalement sous forme d'un prénom féminin.

famous.name: Prince Nicholas of Greece and Denmark
Prince Nikolaos of Greece and Denmark

nikolaos.meaning_en: Nikolaos is a common Greek given name which means "Victor of People", a compound of νίκη nikē 'victory' and λαός laos 'people'. The connotation is "people's champion" or "conqueror of people". The English form is Nicholas.

nikolaus.meaning_en: Nikolaus is a given name. Notable people with this name include the following:
nikolaus.meaning_fr: Nikolaus, prénom masculin, variante de Nicolas Nikolaus cardinal allemand du XIIe siècle

nikolina.meaning_en: Nikolina is the given name of: Nikolina Angelkova, Bulgarian politician Nikolina Baradić is a Croatian politician Nikolina Božičević, Croatian volleyball player Nikolina Brnjac, Croatian politician Nikolina Grabovac, Croatian basketball player Nikolina Ilijanić, Croatian basketball player Nikolina Moldovan, Serbian sprint canoer Nikolina Plavšić, Serbian footballer Nikolina Ristović, Croatian TV presenter Nikolina Ruseva, Bulgarian sprint canoer Nikolina Shtereva, Bulgarian middle distance runner Nikolina Stepan, Croatian long distance runner Nikolina Tankoucheva, Bulgarian artistic gymnast Nikolina Vukčević, Montenegrin handball player Nikolina Zadravec, Croatian handball player Nikolina may also refer to: "Nikolina", a 1917 song recorded by Hjalmar Peterson.

nikos.meaning_en: Nikos is a Greek given name. It originates from Greek Nikolaos, which means "victory of the people". Although used as a proper first name, Nikos is also a popular nickname of the original Nikolaos or Nicholas.
nikos.meaning_fr: Níkos est un prénom grec. C’est l’abréviation de Nikólaos qui a donné Nicolas en français.

nilay.meaning_en: Nilay is a female given name of Turkish origin. Ay means moon and Nil means the river Nile in Turkish language. The name means Moon of the Nile.

nilda.meaning_en: Nilda is a Hispanic feminine given name.

nils.meaning_en: Nils is a Scandinavian given name, a chiefly Norwegian, Danish, Swedish and Latvian variant of Niels, cognate to Nicholas.
nils.meaning_fr: Nils ou Niels est un prénom masculin d'origine scandinave. Principalement porté en Suède, Norvège, Danemark, et en Islande. Il n'est également pas rare de le voir porté dans certains pays tels que les Pays-Bas, l'Allemagne ou la Finlande.

nima.meaning_en: Nima is a Persian male given name popular in Iran. It is also a popular female given name in India meaning "moon" and is derivative of the Sanskrit given name "Purnima", meaning "full" + "moon".

nina.meaning_en: Nina is a feminine given name with various origins and alternate spellings accordingly. Nina may also serve as a short form of names ending in "-nina/-ina", such as Clementina, Christina, or Giannina.

ninette.meaning_en: Ninette is a feminine given name, which originated as a French diminutive of the name Nina.

nino.meaning_en: Nino is an Italian masculine name, a diminutive of Antonino, Giannino, Saturnino, Severino and names ending in "-nino" as well as of Gaetano and Giovanni. It is also used in Greece, Spain, and the Hispanosphere. In South Slavic countries, Nino is a hypocorism of Ninoslav.
nino.meaning_fr: Nino est un prénom, tantôt masculin, tantôt féminin. Il est fêté le 15 décembre.

ninon.meaning_en: Ninon is a French diminutive for names such as Anne that is also in use as an independent name.

nirav.meaning_en: Nirav or Neerav means "quiet or calm." The name Neerav is derived from Sanskrit. In Hindu origin, the meaning of name Neerav is "silent". This name commonly used by Hindus. It is widely used in Bengali, Gujarati, Punjabi, Sanskrit, and Malayalam.

nisa.meaning_fr: Nisa est un prénom féminin turc et, plus rarement, une variante de prénoms féminins tels qu'Agnès ou Denise. C'est par ailleurs une transcription du prénom masculin « Niša » originaire du Monténégro.

nishant.meaning_en: Nishānt or Nishanth is an Indian male name derived from the sandhi of Sanskrit words niśā meaning ‘night’ and anta meaning ‘end’, lit. 'End of night'.

nita.meaning_en: Nita is a given name. It is also a short form of the given names Juanita and Bonita.

nitin.meaning_en: Nitin or Nithin is a male first name in India and Nepal.

nivea.meaning_en: Nivea or Nívea is a feminine given name.

nnamdi.meaning_en: Nnamdi is an Igbo male given name. It means "my father lives".

noah.meaning_en: Noah is historically an English male given name derived from the Biblical figure Noah in Hebrew. It is most likely of Hebrew in origin from the root word "nuach”/“nuakh”, meaning rest.

noam.meaning_en: Noam is a Hebrew name that means "gentleness", "pleasantness" or "peacefulness". It started as the male version of Na'omi, but today is a very common Hebrew name for people of any gender. The common name day is 7 December.
noam.meaning_fr: Noam est prénom masculin d'origine hébraïque, forme masculine de Noémie.

noble.meaning_en: Noble is the given name of the following people: Noble David Cook, author and historian of colonial Peru Noble Craig, American actor and Vietnam War veteran Noble Doss, American National Football League halfback Noble S.

noela.meaning_en: Noela is a feminine given name. It is a variant of Noel.

noelani.meaning_en: Noelani is a Hawaiian female given name, meaning "heavenly mist". People with the given name Noelani include: Noelani Arista, Hawaiian and American historian Noelani Goodyear-Ka'opua, Kanaka Maoli scholar and educator Noelani Pantastico is a Hawaiian-born ballet dancer

noella.meaning_en: Noella is a feminine given name. It is related to the name Noelle.

noelle.meaning_en: Noelle or Noëlle is the feminine form of the unisex name Noel. It derives from the old French Noël, "Christmas," a variant of nael, which itself derives from the Latin natalis, "birthday".

noemie.meaning_en: Noémie is a female name of Hebrew origin, derived from the Hebrew "Na'omi", meaning graceful, beautiful or beauty. Uncommon variant spellings in French include Noëmie. In abbreviated form Noemie or Noemi can be addressed as Noe, Nomi, or in baby form Noemini.
noemie.meaning_fr: Noémie est un prénom biblique féminin d'origine hébraïque. Il vient de l'hébreu Naomi qui signifie « aimable, agréable, gracieuse ». Les Noémie se fêtent le 21 aoûtet 24 décembre

nolan.meaning_en: Nolan is a male given name of Irish origin meaning "champion".

nolberto.meaning_en: Nolberto is a masculine given name. Notable people with the name include: Nolberto Herrera, Mexican journalist Nolberto Molina, Colombian footballer and manager Nolberto Solano, Peruvian footballer and manager

nolwen.meaning_fr: Nolwen ou Nolwenn est un prénom masculin ou féminin de tradition bretonne.

nolwenn.meaning_fr: Nolwen, Nolween ou Nolwenn est un nom propre qui peut désigner :

nonnie.meaning_en: Nonnie is a given name. Notable people with the name include: Nonnie Griffin, Canadian actress Nonnie Moore, American fashion editor

noora.meaning_en: Noora is a female given name in Finnish and Arabic, which is derived from Nora. Notable people with the name include:
noora.meaning_fr: Noora est un prénom féminin pouvant désigner:

nora.meaning_en: Nora or Norah is a feminine given name. It mainly originates as a short form of Honora, a common Anglo-Norman name, ultimately derived from the Latin word Honor. In Hungary, the name Nóra originates as a short form of Eleonóra.
nora.meaning_fr: Le prénom féminin Nora est un emprunt à l'anglais Nora, diminutif de prénoms comme Eleonora, ou Honora. On le retrouve fréquemment dans les pays anglophones, les pays scandinaves, les pays latins, en Allemagne et en Europe de l'Est.

norah.meaning_fr: Norah est un prénom féminin. C'est une variante anglo-saxonne de Nora. On le retrouve fréquemment dans les pays anglophones.

norbert.meaning_en: Norbert is a Germanic given name and infrequent surname, from nord "north" and berht "bright".

nordine.meaning_en: Nur al-Din is a male Arabic given name, translating to 'light of Faith', nūr meaning 'light' and dīn meaning 'religion'. More recently, the name has also been used as a surname. There are many Romanized spelling variants of the name.

noreen.meaning_en: Noreen is an Irish given name, anglicised from Nóirín. It is also an Arabic name with the forms Nourine, Noureen, and Noorin. Another spelling is Norene, Norine and Norinne.

norine.meaning_en: Norine is a given name. Notable people with the name include: Norine Braithwaite, English athlete Norine Burgess, Canadian singer Norine Hammond, American politician Norine G. Johnson, American psychologist Norine Kasperik, American politician

norm.meaning_en: Norm is a masculine given name, most often a short form of Norman.

norma.meaning_en: Norma is a female name. It is of Germanic and Romance origin. A single instance of the name Norma is recorded 1203, where it perhaps derives from the Latin word norma, meaning "precept".

norris.meaning_en: The given name Norris is mainly used in the United States.

norwood.meaning_en: Norwood is a masculine given name.

nosson.meaning_fr: Nosson, Noussen ou Noussin est la prononciation yiddish du prénom Nathan. Nosson Scherman, éditeur général des éditions ArtScroll Mesorah Nosson Zvi Finkel, le rosh yeshiva de Slobodka et son descendant, le rosh yeshiva de Mir

noura.meaning_en: Noura is an Arabic-origin female given name and a surname, derived from the name Noor, meaning "light". People with the name include:

nourdine.meaning_en: Nur al-Din is a male Arabic given name, translating to 'light of Faith', nūr meaning 'light' and dīn meaning 'religion'. More recently, the name has also been used as a surname. There are many Romanized spelling variants of the name.

noureddine.meaning_en: Nur al-Din is a male Arabic given name, translating to 'light of Faith', nūr meaning 'light' and dīn meaning 'religion'. More recently, the name has also been used as a surname. There are many Romanized spelling variants of the name.

nouria.meaning_en: Nouria is a female given name.

nourredine.meaning_en: Nur al-Din is a male Arabic given name, translating to 'light of Faith', nūr meaning 'light' and dīn meaning 'religion'. More recently, the name has also been used as a surname. There are many Romanized spelling variants of the name.

nova.meaning_en: Nova is a unisex given name of Latin origin meaning "new". It is in regular use for both males and females. In the United States, the name has been in use since the 1800s.

novak.meaning_en: Novak and Novák is a surname and masculine given name, derived from the Slavic word for 'new', which usually translates as 'novice', 'new man', 'newcomer'. In most languages, the stress is on the first syllable of the word.

noelie.meaning_en: Noelie is a feminine given name. Alternative spellings include Noélie and Noëlie.

nuno.meaning_en: Nuno is a Portuguese male name, derived either from Latin nunnus 'grandfather' or nonnus 'chamberlain, squire'. It is quite popular in the Portuguese-speaking countries and communities. Its Spanish equivalent is Nuño.

nur.meaning_en: Noor is a common Arabic unisex given name meaning 'light', from the Arabic al-Nur. Feminine variants include Noora, Nora, Norah, Noura, and Nura. It is also used as a surname.

nelio.meaning_en: Nelio is a name. Notable people with the name include:

oakley.meaning_en: Oakley is a unisex given name of English origin that is a transferred use of an English place name and surname meaning “oak clearing”.

obadiah.meaning_en: Obadiah is a masculine given name. It is of Biblical Hebrew origin, and its popularity derives from Obadiah, a prophet in the Hebrew Bible and in the religious traditions of Christianity, Judaism, and Islam.

octavia.meaning_en: Octavia is a feminine given name of Latin origin meaning eight that derives from the Octavia gens.

octavio.meaning_en: Octavio is a Spanish language masculine given name. In the Portuguese language the given name Octavio or Octávio is also found, but in Portuguese the normal spelling is Otávio. It is also used as a surname in the Philippines.
octavio.meaning_fr: Octavio est un prénom espagnol et portugais.

odelia.meaning_en: Odelia or Odilia is a feminine given name. It is a variant form of the name Ottilie. It is also a modern Hebrew name meaning "I will thank Yahweh."

odessa.meaning_en: Odessa is a unisex given name. People with the name include:

odette.meaning_en: Odette is a French given name; Old German name Oda + diminutive -tte; a female form of Odo, Odet.

odile.meaning_fr: Odile est un prénom féminin, dérivé du prénom médiéval Odilia, lui-même construit sur la base germanique od-, qui signifie biens, richesse, d'où prospérité et félicité. Il est fêté le 14 décembre en référence à sainte Odile, patronne de l'Alsace.

ofelia.meaning_en: Ophelia is a feminine given name, probably derived from the Ancient Greek word ὠφέλεια. The name is best known as a character from William Shakespeare's Hamlet who has a tragic end.

oihana.meaning_fr: Oihana est un prénom féminin basque qui signifie « bois, forêt ». L'équivalent de ce prénom en français est « Sylvie ».

oisin.meaning_en: Oisín is an Irish male given name; meaning "fawn" or "little deer", derived from the Irish word os + -ín. It is sometimes anglicized as Osheen or spelt without the acute accent, as Oisin.

oksana.meaning_en: Oksana, Oxana, or Aksana, is a female given name of Ukrainian origin. The closest equivalent is the Russian name Kseniya, but the two names coexist in use in both countries, and neither of them is a shortening of the other.
oksana.meaning_fr: Oksana est un prénom féminin ukrainien. Il est porté entre autres par : Oksana Akinchina, une actrice russe née en 1987. Oksana Baiul, une patineuse artistique ukrainienne née en 1977. Oksana Khvostenko, une biathlète ukrainienne née en 1977.

olaf.meaning_en: Olaf or Olav is a Dutch, Polish, Scandinavian and German given name. It is presumably of Proto-Norse origin, reconstructed as *Anu-laibaz, from anu "ancestor, grand-father" and laibaz "heirloom, descendant". Old English forms are attested as Ǣlāf, Anlāf.

olajuwon.meaning_en: Olajuwon is a surname of Yoruba origin. Notable people with the surname include: Abi Olajuwon, Nigerian-American basketball player and coach, daughter of Hakeem Hakeem Olajuwon, Nigerian-American basketball player

olamide.meaning_en: Ọlámidé is a unisex given name of Yoruba origin meaning "a combination of prestige, success and wealth has arrived".

ole.meaning_en: Ole is a Danish and Norwegian masculine given name, derived from the Old Norse name Óláfr, meaning "ancestor's descendant". Notable people with the given name include:

oleg.meaning_en: Oleg, Oleh, or Aleh is an East Slavic given name. The name is very common in Russia, Ukraine, and Belаrus.
oleg.meaning_fr: Oleg est un prénom slave d’origine scandinave, importé en Rus' de Kiev autour du Xe siècle par les Varègues, et dérivé de l'anthroponyme norrois Helgi . Ce prénom se rencontre surtout chez les Slaves orientaux.

olena.meaning_en: Olena, Olenna is a Ukrainian variant of the feminine name Helen, further equivalent to Elena It is of Greek origin and means "sun ray" or "shining light", see "Helen" for its history.

famous.name: Grand Duchess Olga Nikolaevna of Russia
Grand Duchess Olga Alexandrovna of Russia
Princess Olga of Greece and Denmark

olga.meaning_en: Olga is a Russian feminine given name of Scandinavian origin. It is the equivalent of Helga, and derived from the Old Norse adjective heilagr. The name was brought by Scandinavian settlers who founded Kievan Rus' in the 9th century.

olive.meaning_en: Olive is a feminine given name of English origin meaning olive tree. The name is associated with peace because of the symbolism of the olive branch. An olive wreath has traditionally been worn by champions as a symbol of victory. It has also been seen as a symbol of fruitfulness.

oliver.meaning_en: Oliver is a masculine given name of Old French and Medieval British origin. The name has been generally associated with the Latin term olivarius, meaning "olive tree planter", or "olive branch bearer".
oliver.meaning_fr: Oliver est la variante anglophone, germanique et poitevine du prénom masculin Olivier. Oliver est aussi présent dans la toponymie et l'onomastique de l'aire catalane ; la forme catalane Olivé se prononce aussi à peu près comme le poitevin.

olivette.meaning_en: Olivette is a feminine given name and feminine form of Oliver. Notable people with the name include: Olivette Bice, Vanuatuan sprinter Olivette Miller, American musician Olivette Otele, historian at Bristol University Olivette Thibault, Canadian stage, film and television actress

oliwier.meaning_en: Oliwier is a Polish masculine given name form of Oliver. Notable people with the name include: Oliwier Bednarek, Polish basketball player Oliwier Mutwil, Polish athlete Oliwier Sławiński, Polish footballer Oliwier Wojciechowski, Polish footballer Oliwier Zych, Polish footballer

ollie.meaning_en: Ollie is a given name and a nickname, often as a shortened form of Oliver, Olive, Olympia, Olga, or Olivia. Variants include Olie, Oli, Oly, and Olly.

oluwaseun.meaning_en: Oluwaseun is a given name. Notable people with the name include: Oluwaseun Adegbola, Nigerian footballer Oluwaseun A. Aderogba, Anglican bishop of Jebba Oluwaseun Osowobi, Nigerian women's rights activist Oluwaseun Oluwatosin Otukpe, British musician known as S.O.

oluwaseyi.meaning_en: Seyi, Oluseyi, or Oluwaseyi is a Yoruba unisex given name and an occasional surname.It means"does it".

oluwatobiloba.meaning_en: Oluwatobiloba or Olúwatóbilọ́ba is a common unisex name of yoruba origin. It means The lord is great a king. A diminutive form of the name is Olúwatóbi which means The lord is great / big.

olympia.meaning_en: Olympia is a feminine given name.

omar.meaning_en: Omar is the most common Arabic rendition of a series of names, predominantly masculine given names, originating in the Arabic language.

omer.meaning_en: Omar is the most common Arabic rendition of a series of names, predominantly masculine given names, originating in the Arabic language.

onur.meaning_en: Onur is a common Turkish given name and a surname. In Turkish, "Onur" means "Honour" or Pride. Its origin comes from Latin "honor, honōrem", most resembling the word honneur in French or onore in Italian. Notable people with the name include:

oona.meaning_en: Oona is a feminine given name. It is an anglicisation of the Irish-language name Úna. Apart from in Ireland, it is also a popular name in Finland.
oona.meaning_fr: Oona est un prénom féminin pouvant désigner:

opal.meaning_en: Opal is a primarily feminine given name derived from the name of the gemstone opal. The gemstone is the birthstone for October. Its name is derived from the Sanskrit upala, which means 'jewel'. It came into use along with other gemstone names during the late Victorian era.

ophelia.meaning_en: Ophelia is a feminine given name, probably derived from the Ancient Greek word ὠφέλεια. The name is best known as a character from William Shakespeare's Hamlet who has a tragic end.

ora.meaning_en: Ora is the given name of: Ora Alexander, American classic female blues singer Ora Anlen, Israeli Paralympic athlete in various sports Ora Carew, American silent film actress Ora Collard, American businessman and politician Ora Graves, US Navy sailor and Medal of Honor recipient Ora Haibe, American race car driver Ora Kedem, Austrian-born Israeli chemist and academic Ora Larthard, American cellist Ora Lassila, Finnish computer scientist Ora McMurry, United States Army Air Service pilot during World War I Ora Namir, Israeli former politician and diplomat Ora Nichols, American pioneer of radio sound effects Ora A.

orelia.meaning_en: Orelia or its variants Orelious, Ornellas, Orellana, Orellia, Ortelius or Orelias is a feminine name primarily found in Europe, Mediterranean countries and South America. Deriving from the Latin Aurelius family meaning "golden".

oreoluwa.meaning_en: Oreoluwa is a Nigerian unisex given name with Yoruba origins, meaning "a gift from God". It is similar in meaning to Olubunmi, Ebunoluwa and Onyinyechi.

oreste.meaning_en: Oreste is an Italian masculine given name. It is derived from the Orestes, who in Greek mythology is the son of Clytemnestra and Agamemnon.

orhan.meaning_en: Orhan is a Turkish surname and masculine given name that means Khan of the fortress. Notable people with the name include:

ori.meaning_en: Ori is a gender-neutral Hebrew given name, which means "my light”. Also a name from the Hebrew Bible. A female name with a similar meaning and sound is Orit.

oriana.meaning_en: Oriana is a given name meaning 'gold, sunrise, or dawn'. Variants include Orianna, Oriane or Orianne. Sometimes Orian, Orestes or Dorian may be a male given name or a family name, as Orians, Oriani, or Doria.
oriana.meaning_fr: Dans les langues européennes, Oriane est un prénom féminin.

orin.meaning_en: Orin is an anglicised spelling of the Irish given name Odhrán, historically spelled Oḋrán.

orion.meaning_fr: Orion est un prénom d'origine grecque, porté essentiellement en Grèce, aux États-Unis, et avec une popularité grandissante en France.

orla.meaning_en: Orla is an anglicisation of Órfhlaith, a feminine given name of Irish origin. The name is often interpreted as meaning "golden princess", as it is derived from the Irish words ór and flaith.

orlando.meaning_en: Orlando is a masculine given name, originally an Italian form of the given name Roland.

orli.meaning_en: Orli is a feminine given name, meaning "my light" in Hebrew. It may also be a nickname for the masculine name Orlando.

orly.meaning_en: Orly is a unisex given name.

ornella.meaning_en: Ornella is an Italian feminine given name, probably derived from ornello, "flowering ash tree". It was coined by Gabriele D'Annunzio in his 1904 play The Daughter of Iorio and popularized by the fame of singer Ornella Vanoni and, later, of actress Ornella Muti.

orren.meaning_en: Orren is the name of: Orren Bennett, American soldier who fought in the American Civil War Orren D. Casselman, Ontario merchant and political figure Orren C. Moore, U.S. Representative from New Hampshire Orren Stephenson, Australian rules footballer Orren R.

orrin.meaning_en: Orin is an anglicised spelling of the Irish given name Odhrán, historically spelled Oḋrán.

orso.meaning_fr: Orso est un prénom italien. Il est également répandu en Corse, bien que la forme traditionnelle corse soit Orsu, -u étant l'équivalent du -o italien. Son usage est censé protéger les enfants ainsi nommés du « mauvais œil ».

osama.meaning_en: Osama, also spelt Osamah, Oussama, Usama, and other variants, is an Arabic masculine given name. The name derives from the same stem of the noun اسم ism "name", and means more or less "the one with a name"; it also has the additional meaning of "lion".

osborne.meaning_en: Osborne , along with Osbourne, Osbern, Osborn and Usborne, is an English name cognate with, and possibly influenced by the Old Norse Ásbjørn. The English Os and the Norse Ás mean God, while bjørn means bear in Norse.

oscar.meaning_en: Oscar or Oskar is a masculine given name of English, Old Norse and Irish origin.

osian.meaning_en: Osian is a Welsh masculine given name, derived from the Irish legendary poet and warrior Oisín. The name is derived from the Irish for "little deer". Osian was the 22nd most popular name for baby boys in Wales in 2017.

oskar.meaning_en: Oscar or Oskar is a masculine given name of English, Old Norse and Irish origin.

osman.meaning_en: Osman refers to two different names: Osman or Usman is the Turkish, Persian, and Urdu transliteration of the Arabic masculine given name Uthman.

osmin.meaning_fr: Osmin est un prénom masculin porté par : Osmin Gardey, né Jean Ozemin Gardey à Maubourguet le 13 décembre 1836 et décédé le 27 janvier 1914 dans sa commune de naissance : curé parisien.

oswald.meaning_en: Oswald is a masculine given name, from Old English Osƿeald, from os "god" and ƿeald "rule". The Old High German cognate was Answald, the Old Norse form was Ásvaldr. Oswald of Northumbria was a king of Northumbria and is venerated as saint.

otelia.meaning_en: Ottilie is a feminine given name. It is a French derivative of the medieval German masculine name Otto and, like other related Germanic names beginning with the prefixes Ad-, Aut-, Od-, Ot-, Oth-, or Ud-, has the meaning "prosperous in battle", "riches", "prosperous" or "wealth".

otha.meaning_en: Otha is a given name and surname. Notable persons with that name include:

othman.meaning_en: Uthman, also spelled Othman, is a male Arabic given name with the literal meaning of a young wise, brave, Wise, or brave. It is popular as a male given name among Muslims.

othniel.meaning_en: Othniel is the name of the first of the Biblical Judges. It can also be a given name. Notable people with the given name include: Othniel Dossevi, Togolese footballer Othniel Looker, American politician from Ohio and member of the Democratic-Republican Party.

otilia.meaning_en: Otilia is a feminine given name.
otilia.meaning_fr: Otilia est un prénom féminin roumain. C'est également un nom de famille.

otis.meaning_en: Otis is a male given name derived from an English surname, which was in turn derived from Ode, a variant form of Odo and Otto. The name also has origins in the Ars Goetia, it is a variation of the name Botis.

ottis.meaning_en: Ottis is a surname and masculine given name.

otto.meaning_en: Otto is a masculine German given name and a surname. It originates as an Old High German short form of Germanic names beginning in aud-, an element meaning "wealth, prosperity". The name is recorded from the 7th century.
otto.meaning_fr: Pour l'ensemble des articles sur les personnes portant ce prénom, consulter : la liste des articles dont le titre commence par ce prénom les listes produites par Wikidata : Liste des personnes de prénom « Otto » — même liste en incluant les éventuels prénoms composés qui contiennent « Otto ».

oumar.meaning_en: Omar is the most common Arabic rendition of a series of names, predominantly masculine given names, originating in the Arabic language.

oumou.meaning_fr: Oumou, est un prénom féminin d'Afrique subsaharienne dérivé de l'arabe ’umm : « mère ». Ce prénom se rencontre surtout en Afrique de l'Ouest.

ousmane.meaning_fr: Ousmane, prénom masculin d’Afrique subsaharienne, équivalent de l’arabe Othman, prénom du troisième calife de l’islam, Uthman ben Affan.

ovidio.meaning_en: Ovidio is a given name. Notable people with the name include: Ovidio G.

oz.meaning_en: Oz is the given name or nickname of: Given name: Oz Almog, Israeli–Austrian artist Oz Almog, Israeli sociologist and historian Oz Blayzer, Israeli basketball player Oz Ifrah, Israeli football player Oz Pearlman, American magician Oz Peretz, Israeli footballer Oz Raly, Israeli footballer Nickname: Osman Oz Bengur, American investment banker and politician Robert Oz Clarke, British wine writer Richard Oz Griebel, American banker, lawyer and politician Osborne Oz Scott, American film, television and theatre director and television producer

ozell.meaning_en: Ozell is both a given name and a surname.

pablo.meaning_en: Pablo is a masculine given name, the Spanish form of the name Paul.

paco.meaning_en: Paco is a Spanish nickname for Francisco.

paddy.meaning_en: Paddy is a unisex given name. It is often short for Patrick, Patricia, or Pádraig. Notable people include:
